informal.Erdos548.marked_word_gluing_count: For a permutation-closed family W of repetition-free words, all of the same length m, and families A, B, C of letter sets with C ⊆ A and A R ∧ B X → C (R ∪ X) for disjoint R, X, the marked cuts (l, k) with l ∈ W and k ≤ m qualifying for A plus those qualifying for B number at most the allowed cuts plus those qualifying for C.

records.title: Finitely generated cones and finite LP duality
records.abstract: Proves that finitely generated cones in real normed spaces are closed, including a conic Carathéodory reduction and PointedCone API forms. Derives a finite-dimensional inequality form of Farkas' lemma and proves packing attainment with equality to the covering infimum for finite covering and packing linear programs. The Farkas and LP statements overlap the pooled Duality development; the generic cone-closedness results provide the project's distinct reusable API.

informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.fg_cone_is: The cone generated by a finite family in a real normed vector space is a closed set.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.farkas_ge: An infeasible finite system of nonnegative linear inequalities admits a nonnegative separating Farkas certificate.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.covering_p: Given a finite nonnegative matrix with a strictly positive entry in every column and nonnegative capacities, there is a feasible nonnegative packing whose unit-objective value is maximal and equals the infimum cost of nonnegative coverings with unit demand.

records.title: Chordal graphs: minimal separators and simplicial vertices
records.abstract: A reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Paper II: defines chordal graphs through the cycle-and-chord characterization, proves induced-subgraph heredity and the clique property for finite minimal separators of fixed vertex pairs, proves Dirac's simplicial-vertex theorem, and proves the connected non-complete case of the two-vertex conclusion.

informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.comap: A graph that embeds as an induced subgraph of a chordal graph is itself chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.induce: Every induced subgraph of a chordal graph is chordal.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.minimalSeparator_i: Every finite minimal separator of two fixed vertices in a chordal graph is a clique.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_isSimplicia: Every nonempty finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex.
informal.SimpleGraph.IsChordal.exists_two_nonadj_: Every connected non-complete finite chordal graph has two non-adjacent simplicial vertices.

records.title: Near-perfect triangle packings from sum-zero triples
records.abstract: Records a reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Paper III: pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in any finite complete graph such that every vertex is incident to at most three uncovered edges, using a cyclic-group sum-zero triple system, with a bridge to Mathlib's SimpleGraph API.

informal.SumZeroTriangles.exists_simpleGraph_tria: For every finite vertex type, its complete simple graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangle graphs whose uncovered graph has degree at most three at every vertex.
informal.SumZeroTriangles.exists_triangle_packing: Every finite complete graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles leaving uncovered degree at most three at every vertex.

records.title: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
records.abstract: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.

informal.Erdos865.erdos865_upper_bound: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).
informal.Erdos865.erdos865_contains_triple: Every A ⊆ [1,N] with 5·N + 53 < 8·|A| contains a pairwise-sum triple (the paper's Theorem 1.1 form).
informal.Erdos865.sharpness: For N = 8M with M ≥ 1 there is a triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] with 8·|A| = 5·N + 16, so the constant 5/8 is optimal.

records.title: Even graphs are edge-disjoint unions of cycles
records.abstract: Decomposes every finite loopless edge set with even degree at each vertex into edge-disjoint simple cycles and derives a simultaneous fixed-point-free pairing of incident edges.

informal.Finset.exists_cycleDecomp: Every finite loopless edge set whose degree is even at every vertex is the edge-disjoint union of simple cycles of length at least three.
informal.Finset.exists_edge_pairing_of_even: If every vertex has even degree, then the incident edges at every vertex admit a simultaneous fixed-point-free involutive pairing.

records.title: Event Structures and Causal-Consistent Reversibility
records.abstract: Formalizes event structures with binary conflict, their configurations, computations, the trace monoid, and causal-consistent reversibility, proving correctness and causal-safety of rollback, uniqueness of minimal and maximal replays, and conditional replay-existence characterizations.

informal.EventStructures.EventStructure: Defines an event structure as a partially ordered set of events with an irreflexive symmetric conflict relation.
informal.EventStructures.Conf: Defines a configuration as a conflict-free, downward-closed set of events.
informal.EventStructures.Rollback.rollback_correc: Proves that the original configuration is reachable from the rollback of an event when the configuration is finitely representable.
informal.EventStructures.Rollback.rollback_causal: Proves causal safety of rollback - events causally after the rolled-back event are removed.
informal.EventStructures.Replay.minReplay_unique: Proves uniqueness of the minimal replay of a log - any two minimal replays compatible with the log reach the same configuration.
informal.EventStructures.Trace.TraceMonoid: Defines the trace monoid as lists of events quotiented by the congruence generated by swapping adjacent concurrent events; paths in the configuration graph are quotiented by the same trace equivalence to form asynchronous paths.

records.title: Chaos and the Julia set of the complex exponential
records.abstract: Formalizes the dynamics of z ↦ exp(z): escaping points, points with dense forward orbit, and repelling periodic points are dense in the complex plane; the map is chaotic in Devaney's sense and its Julia set is the whole plane. The development proves eventual covering of every compact set omitting zero, constructs contracting inverse branches, and rules out every locally uniform spherical subsequential limit on nonempty open sets. It includes general normal-sequence restriction lemmas, quantitative open mapping, and a two-target obstruction for arbitrary separated uniform codomains. The Lean proofs were primarily generated by AI under Lasse Rempe's direction. The initial six-lemma architecture adapts John Harrison's HOL Light formalization, credited with its retained BSD notice in the entry module.

informal.ExpChaotic.devaney_chaotic: The complex exponential is continuous, has dense periodic points, and the monoid action generated by its iterates is topologically transitive on the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.juliaSet_exp: The Julia set of the complex exponential is the whole plane, where the Fatou set is defined by local normality of sphere-valued iterates with arbitrary locally uniform sphere-valued limits.
informal.ExpChaotic.dense_repellingPeriodicSet: Points p with a positive period n and derivative norm greater than one for the nth exponential iterate are dense in the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.eventually_covers_compact: For every nonempty open set U in the complex plane and every compact set K omitting zero, all sufficiently large iterates of the exponential map send U onto a set containing K.
informal.ExpChaotic.dense_escapingSet: Points whose forward exponential orbit eventually leaves every centered Euclidean ball are dense in the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.not_countable_denseOrbitSet: The set of complex points with dense forward exponential orbit is uncountable.
informal.ExpChaotic.not_tendstoLocallyUniformly_s: On every nonempty open set in the complex plane, no strictly increasing subsequence of exponential iterates converges locally uniformly to any function into the Riemann sphere.

records.title: Factorization Systems
records.abstract: Formalizes factorization systems, orthogonality, orthogonal complements, and the standard construction from weak factorization plus orthogonality.

informal.CategoryTheory.FactorizationSystem: Defines factorization systems on a category with specified left and right classes.
informal.CategoryTheory.FactorizationSystemCharac: Constructs a factorization system from repleteness, weak factorizations, and orthogonality.
informal.CategoryTheory.orthogonal: Defines orthogonality of two morphisms by existence and uniqueness of diagonal fillers.
informal.CategoryTheory.right_orthogonal_compleme: Defines the right orthogonal complement of a morphism property.

records.title: Feige's sharp unit-slack inequality
records.abstract: For small-universe probability spaces, proves the sharp fixed-dimensional unit-slack lower bound for sums of independent nonnegative random variables: if each coordinate has mean at most one, then the probability that the sum lies below its mean plus one is at least (n/(n+1))^n, and this constant is optimal. The supporting library formalizes the Vlassis--Thomas exact distribution-free calibration theorem, Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality and sharp simplex example, and the normalized-exponential bridge joining them.

informal.Feige.sharp_unit_slack_feige_complete: For every positive dimension n and every small-universe probability space, the sharp fixed-dimensional lower bound for the strict event that a sum of independent nonnegative random variables is below its expectation plus one is (n/(n+1))^n, and an explicit finite family proves optimality.
informal.VlassisThomas.exactCalibration: On every small-universe probability space, the Dirichlet statistic used in the proof is super-uniform for every independent family of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables whose coordinate means are at most one.
informal.Grunbaum.grunbaum_centroid_halfspace: Every closed halfspace containing the centroid of a positive-volume convex body in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains at least the sharp Grünbaum fraction of the body's volume.

records.title: Fel's Conjecture on Syzygies of Numerical Semigroups
records.abstract: Formalizes Fel's conjectural formula for syzygies of numerical semigroups.

informal.fels_conjecture: Proves Fel's conjecture for the polynomial attached to numerical-semigroup syzygies.

records.title: FinEqs - reducing equations defining a subset of n-space over a finite field
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite-field equation-reduction theorem and sharpness examples.

informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.theorem_1: Reduces equations on a small finite set to at most n equations in the same span.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.prop_1: Shows the cardinality bound in the reduction theorem is sharp.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.corollary_2: Applies the reduction theorem to affine space over a finite field.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.corollary_3: Applies the reduction theorem to nonempty projective zero loci.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.remark_example: Shows n - 1 coordinate-function combinations have at least q common zeros.

records.title: Fundamental groups of finite connected graphs
records.abstract: Constructs the standard interval-cell realization of a finite connected directed multigraph and proves that its topological fundamental group is a free group of rank E - V + 1. The proof uses an explicit spanning-tree basis and develops a verified path-lifting cover, a contraction of the covering tree, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding free-abelian result.

informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphTopologicalFun: For a finite weakly connected directed multigraph, the topological fundamental group of its interval-cell quotient realization at any vertex is explicitly isomorphic to the free group on E + 1 - V generators.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphCombinatorialT: The endomorphism group at a vertex in the graph's free groupoid is explicitly isomorphic to the topological fundamental group of the interval-cell realization.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphCoverProjectio: The canonical path-lifting projection from rooted free-groupoid paths to graph vertices is a quiver covering, with bijective maps on every incoming and outgoing edge star.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphRealization_tr: The interval-cell realization of a directed arborescence is simply connected, via an explicit continuous contraction to its root.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphFundamentalGro: The combinatorial fundamental group is trivial exactly when the graph's cycle rank E + 1 - V is zero.
The additive abelianization of the graph fundamental group is the free abelian group on E + 1 - V generators.

records.title: Finite max-flow / min-cut
records.abstract: Develops finite networks with real nonnegative capacities, proves cut-flow weak duality and maximum-flow attainment, and derives max-flow/min-cut equality by an augmenting-path argument.

informal.Contrib.MaxFlowMinCut.maxflow_eq_mincut: Every finite network with real nonnegative capacities and distinct source and sink admits a feasible flow and a source-sink cut whose flow value equals the cut capacity.
informal.Contrib.MaxFlowMinCut.value_le_capacity: The value of every feasible flow is at most the capacity of every source-sink cut.
informal.Contrib.MaxFlowMinCut.max_flow_exists: Every finite network with real nonnegative capacities admits a maximum-value feasible flow.

records.title: Sharp Five-Distance and Sup-Norm Gap Theorems
records.abstract: Formalizes sharp gap theorems for Kronecker sequences on tori: the Euclidean five-distance theorem on the 2-torus and the sup-norm gap bound, together with explicit arithmetic witnesses realizing the extremal cases - five distinct nearest-neighbour distances for the Euclidean and sup-norm metrics in dimension two, and nine distinct sup-norm distances in dimension three (Haynes-Marklof-Ramirez), via exact modular arithmetic on best simultaneous Diophantine approximations.

informal.ThreeGap.EuclideanRecords.sharp_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose Euclidean nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the Euclidean five-distance bound is sharp.
informal.ThreeGap.LinftyRecords.sharp_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension two.
informal.ThreeGap.LinftyRecords3.nine_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 3-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize at least nine distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension three.

records.title: The 5/8 theorem
records.abstract: Proves Gustafson's 5/8 theorem — the Mathlib commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8, with the infinite case immediate from commProb being zero — via the finite-group index bounds for the center and centralizers of noncentral elements.

informal.FiveEighths.commProb_le_five_eighths: The commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8.
informal.FiveEighths.centralFraction_le_quarter: The center of a finite nonabelian group contains at most a quarter of its elements.
informal.FiveEighths.centralizerFraction_le_half: The centralizer of a noncentral element of a finite group contains at most half of its elements.

records.title: Flean: Floating-Point Numbers in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes a configurable model of floating-point numbers in Lean 4, including normal and subnormal representations, conversions between rationals and floats, round-trip correctness, and rounding error bounds.

informal.Flean.Float: Defines the floating-point number type parameterized by a precision and exponent configuration, with normal, subnormal, infinite, and NaN cases.
informal.toFloat: Rounds a rational number to the nearest representable floating-point value under a given rounding mode.
informal.toRat: Interprets a floating-point value as the exact rational number it represents.
informal.to_float_to_rat: Proves the round-trip identity that converting a finite nonzero float to a rational and back recovers the original float.
informal.roundf_close: Bounds the distance between a rational and its rounded floating-point representation.

records.title: Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes
records.abstract: Formalizes Kummer's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem for every odd regular prime exponent. The development proves both cases of the theorem and includes the required theory of cyclotomic integers, relative units, Hilbert 90 and 92, ramification, class groups, and Kummer's lemma.

informal.flt_regular: Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every odd regular prime exponent.
informal.FltRegular.caseI: The first case of Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every regular prime: no primitive solution exists when the exponent does not divide the product of the three terms.
informal.FltRegular.caseII: The second case of Fermat's Last Theorem holds for every odd regular prime: no primitive nonzero solution exists when the exponent divides the product of the three terms.
informal.eq_pow_prime_of_unit_of_congruent: A unit of the cyclotomic field of an odd regular prime that is congruent to an integer modulo the prime is itself a prime-th power.

records.title: First Order Language of ZF Set Theory
records.abstract: Formalizes ZF set theory inside Lean's `FirstOrder.Language` framework, enabling meta-mathematical arguments such as elementary submodels.

informal.FirstOrder.ZFC.ModelZF: Bundles the ZF axioms (Emptyset, Pairing, Union, Powerset, Infinity, Regularity, Comprehension, Replacement) into a single model class.
informal.FirstOrder.ZFC.ext_induction: States the principle of mathematical induction over ω externally for any bounded formula in LZFC.

records.title: Formal Learning Theory Kernel
records.abstract: Formalizes major equivalences and separations in PAC, VC, Gold-style, and online learning theory.

informal.vc_characterization: Characterizes PAC learnability by finite VC dimension.
informal.fundamental_theorem: Bundles the central PAC, VC, compression, Rademacher, and sample-complexity equivalences.
informal.fundamental_vc_compression: Relates finite VC dimension to compression with side information.
informal.gold_theorem: States the Gold-style characterization for identification in the limit.
informal.mind_change_characterization: Characterizes learnability by a bounded mind-change ordinal.
informal.littlestone_characterization: Characterizes online learnability by finite Littlestone dimension.
informal.pac_not_implies_online: Separates PAC learnability from online learnability.
informal.ex_not_implies_pac: Separates explanatory learnability from PAC learnability.

records.title: Strengthened V0 Bounded Arithmetic Interfaces
records.abstract: Formalizes first-order and two-sorted bounded-arithmetic model infrastructure, including arithmetic model laws and string-addition laws for strengthened bundled V0-style interfaces with propositional induction, order, cancellation, decidability, and algebraic laws assumed as fields rather than derived from a separate raw V0 class.

informal.IOPENModel.add_assoc: Proves associativity of addition in IOPEN models.
informal.IOPENModel.add_comm: Proves commutativity of addition in IOPEN models.
informal.IDelta0Model.pred_exists: Shows that nonzero elements in IDelta0 models have predecessors.
informal.IDelta0Model.mul_cancel_right: Proves right cancellation for multiplication by a nonzero element in IDelta0 models.
informal.V0Model.xind: Exposes string induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, whose fields include the comprehension and induction/order principles used downstream.
informal.V0Model.ind_strengthened_v0: Exposes propositional induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, rather than deriving it from only the raw finite V0 axiom list.
informal.str_add_comm_strengthened_v0: Proves commutativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.
informal.str_add_assoc_strengthened_v0: Proves associativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle, using the bundled propositional induction field.
informal.str_succ_assoc_strengthened_v0: Proves that string addition associates with string successor in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.

records.title: A 4AP-free permutation of the positive integers
records.abstract: Formalizes Boon Suan Ho's construction of a permutation of the positive integers with no four-term arithmetic progression as a subsequence, proving the binary-order lemmas, extension lemma, and computable limit.

informal.FourAP.exists_fourAPFree_positive_permut: There exists a bijection of the positive integers such that no four increasing positions map to a nonconstant four-term arithmetic progression, including negative common differences.
informal.FourAP.explicitPositivePermutation_apFre: The explicit computable positive-integer permutation constructed in the development has the stated four-term progression avoidance property.

records.title: Maxima of Coxeter frieze patterns are Fibonacci numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the claim that the sequence of maxima of values of (Coxeter) arithmetic frieze patterns is the Fibonacci sequence, using a correspondence between arithmetic frieze patterns and n-flutes.

informal.main3: Proves that the maximum value of an arithmetic frieze pattern of width n is exactly the n-th Fibonacci number, and that this bound is attained.
informal.FluteBounded: Proves that every entry of an n-flute is bounded above by the n-th Fibonacci number.
informal.glideSymm: Proves the glide-reflection symmetry of Coxeter frieze patterns.
informal.translationInvariance: Proves the (n+1)-periodicity (horizontal translation invariance) of Coxeter frieze patterns.

records.title: FrontierMath Ramsey Hypergraphs
records.abstract: Formalizes lower bounds for the Brian-Larson hypergraph extremal function H(n), including a uniform 26/25 improvement over the recursive benchmark k_n for n ≥ 15 and a Lubell-frame asymptotic lower bound.

informal.HypergraphLowerBound.thm_main_H_lower_bo: Proves H(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.uniform_26_25: Proves the uniform recursive construction bound A(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.frame_recurrence: The substitution-frame recurrence that combines block witnesses and a valid support frame into a larger witness.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.lubell_is_frame: Proves that the Lubell support family forms a valid frame for every arity t ≥ 2.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.fixed_t_bound: Derives a fixed-t lower bound for the exact witness supremum from Lubell frames.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.asymptotic_lower_bo: Proves the asymptotic lower bound liminf H(n) / k(n) ≥ 2 * log 2.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.thm_asymptotic: States the asymptotic consequence in terms of H(n) divided by n log n.

records.title: The Fundamental Inequality of Valued Fields
records.abstract: Defines the ramification index and residue degree of an extension of valued fields and proves the fundamental inequality e * f ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions, via the valuation independence of products of coset representatives and residue-field basis lifts.

informal.Valuation.ramificationIndex: Defines the ramification index e(w/v) as the relative index of the value group of the restricted valuation inside the value group of the extension.
informal.Valuation.residueDegree: Defines the residue degree f(w/v) as the rank of the residue field extension.
informal.Valuation.valuation_independence: Elements with valuations in distinct cosets and residues that are linearly independent give products that are linearly independent over the base field.
informal.Valuation.fundamentalInequality: The fundamental inequality e(w/v) * f(w/v) ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions of valued fields.

records.title: Polynomial-factor hardness of the closest vector problem
records.abstract: Formalizes polynomial-factor NP-hardness of the closest vector problem through an explicit reduction from 3-SAT. The development also derives NP-hardness of binary nearest codeword, binary syndrome decoding, and finite p-norm variants of GapCVP. It includes machine-level polynomial-time bounds, binary encodings, affine systems, Reed--Solomon-style interpolation, and the lattice and coding-theory reductions needed by the final results.

informal.GapCVP.Comparator.gapCVP400IsNPHard: GapCVP in the Euclidean norm with approximation factor n^(1/400), where n is the lattice dimension, is NP-hard as a promise problem: every NP language reduces in polynomial time to the promise problem on encoded well-formed instances (positive dimension, nonsingular integer basis, positive rational radius) with an integer target, whose YES instances have a lattice vector within the radius of the target and whose NO instances have every lattice vector at distance greater than n^(1/400) times the radius.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.binaryNearestCodewordI: Binary nearest codeword is NP-hard as a promise problem.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.binarySyndromeDecoding: Binary syndrome decoding is NP-hard as a promise problem.
informal.GapCVP.Comparator.finitePNormGapCVPIsNPH: For every rational p at least one, the finite p-norm version of GapCVP is NP-hard as a promise problem.

records.title: Gaussian Moments Conjecture counterexamples
records.abstract: Proves explicit complex polynomial counterexamples to the Gaussian Moments Conjecture in every dimension at least three, using genuine expectations under finite products of standard real Gaussian measures. Retains reusable polynomial integrability, Stein identities, complex contractions, coefficient formulas, injective-coordinate marginals, and related moment results.

informal.GaussianMomentsCounterexamples.not_GMC_o: For every n at least three, the Gaussian Moments Conjecture fails: some complex polynomial has all positive pure Gaussian moments zero, while a polynomial multiplier prevents eventual mixed-moment vanishing.
informal.GaussianMomentsCounterexamples.master_th: For every complex univariate polynomial A and positive m, the expectation of A(Q3) times P3 to power m equals m! times the degree-m coefficient of A(X) times (1+X) to power m-1. The explicit P3 has degree four and five terms in its natural complex coordinates.
informal.GaussianMomentsCounterexamples.master_fo: The analogous arbitrary-A coefficient identity for the explicit four-variable polynomial P4, of degree three and six terms in its natural complex coordinates, gives an independent counterexample.

records.title: Density-One GKP Divisibility and Its Carry-Language Characterization
records.abstract: Proves that the exponents k satisfying the Graham--Knuth--Patashnik divisibility condition have natural density one. The proof gives an exact all-depth modular sieve, quantitative bounds for possible failures in initial intervals, and a density-zero limit for the failure proportion. It also develops the Kummer digit-sum bridge, the binary-popcount reduction, and a verified ternary carry automaton. The universal GKP conjecture remains open because the possible density-zero failure set may be nonempty.

informal.GKPCarry.tendsto_gkpSuccessProportion_on: The proportion of exponents k below N for which nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 2^k tends to one as N tends to infinity.
informal.GKPCarry.card_gkpFailureExponentsBelow_l: At each ternary depth n+3, the number of possible failures below N is at most (N divided by 2*3^(n+2), plus one) times (n+9)*2^n.
informal.GKPCarry.gkp_exact_modular_sieve: At depth n+3, exactly (n+9)*2^n of the 2*3^(n+2) exponent classes remain uncertified; every other class gives divisibility by nine and avoids the deficient carry language for all exponents in that class.
informal.GKPCarry.gkpConjecture_iff_badCarryLangu: The GKP conjecture is equivalent to the assertion that every nonexceptional power of two avoids the explicitly defined deficient-carry regular language. This is an exact reformulation and does not prove the remaining avoidance assertion.
informal.GKPCarry.nine_dvd_centralBinom_iff_two_l: For every natural number n, its central binomial coefficient is divisible by nine exactly when doubling the canonical ternary expansion of n creates at least two carries.
informal.GKPCarry.badCarryLanguage_true_iff_shape: The deficient-carry automaton accepts exactly three concrete little-endian ternary word shapes: all digits zero or one; a unique top digit two; or a unique two followed by a higher zero with all other digits zero or one.
informal.GKPCarry.card_badCarryWords: Among all ternary words of length n+2, exactly (n+7) times 2^n create fewer than two carries when doubled.
informal.GKPCarry.nine_dvd_centralBinom_four_pow_: For every m from 27 through 6560, nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 4^m; this is a bounded computational corollary, not the headline result.

records.title: Grothendieck's Vanishing Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Grothendieck's vanishing theorem for sheaf cohomology on Noetherian topological spaces.

informal.GrothendieckVanishing: Proves vanishing of sheaf cohomology above the topological Krull dimension.

records.title: Known Bounds for the Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
records.abstract: Formalizes the currently known bounds 5 <= chi(R^2) <= 7 for the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane. The upper bound constructs an explicit Isbell-style seven-coloring. The lower bound checks Parts' 481-vertex coloring certificate, develops a finite doubled triangular-lattice forcing gadget, proves its exact Euclidean embedding, and closes the four-color contradiction with a spindle construction. The exact chromatic number remains open.

informal.HadwigerNelsonBounds.hadwiger_nelson_kno: The chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane lies between five and seven, inclusive.
informal.HadwigerNelsonBounds.unitDistanceGraph_n: The unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane admits no proper coloring with four colors.
informal.HadwigerNelsonBounds.chromaticNumber_le_: An explicit Isbell-style coloring proves that the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane is colorable with seven colors.

records.title: The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms
records.abstract: Proves the finite-dimensional Hanson-Wright concentration inequality for quadratic forms of independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian real random variables whose maximum least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scale is positive, for matrices with positive Frobenius and operator norms. The bound uses the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2). This is the MGF normalization of the usual result; no formal identification with an Orlicz psi-2 norm is claimed. The development derives the required moment-generating-function certificate instead of assuming it, and contributes reusable scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum infrastructure.

informal.LeanPool.HansonWright.hanson_wright_ineq: For independent mean-zero real random variables with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales and positive maximum coordinate MGF scale, and a matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, the centered quadratic form satisfies the Hanson-Wright two-regime exponential tail bound with the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2).
informal.LeanPool.HansonWright.hasHansonWrightMGF: Given positive K and operator norm and C at least 64 * exp(1)^2, independent coordinates with global-MGF sub-Gaussian parameter K^2 satisfy the local quadratic cumulant-generating-function estimate needed for Hanson-Wright.
informal.LeanPool.bernstein_inequality: A finite family of independent, centered, uniformly bounded real random variables satisfies the classical scalar Bernstein tail inequality.

records.title: A complex structure on the six-sphere
records.abstract: Formalizes Levent Alpöge's construction of a complex-analytic atlas on the standard six-sphere. The development builds a compact complex threefold from torus fibrations with cusp and elliptic fibres, computes its homology and fundamental group, proves that its underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the six-sphere, and transports the complex atlas across that homeomorphism. It adapts Lean developments by Yury G. Kudryashov and Sebastian Kumar, together with the statement from the Formal Conjectures Authors.

informal.Mathoverflow1973.SixSphereComplexAtlas.e: The standard unit six-sphere admits a complex three-dimensional charted-space structure making it a complex-analytic manifold.
The standard unit six-sphere admits a complex three-dimensional charted-space structure making it a continuously differentiable complex manifold.
informal.Mathoverflow1973.mathoverflow_1973: The formalized statement of MathOverflow question 1973: the standard six-sphere carries a complex three-dimensional manifold atlas.

records.title: Homogeneous self-dual interior-point method for linear programming
records.abstract: Formalizes a homogeneous self-dual interior-point method for linear programming, including primal-dual data, Newton block solvability from full row rank, fixed Ye-Todd-Mizuno predictor/corrector local estimates, contraction bounds, and logarithmic stopping certificates for generated iterates.

informal.HSDInteriorPointLP.YTM_fixed_local_theor: Packages the fixed Ye-Todd-Mizuno local theory, combining predictor and corrector estimates for the tight and wide central neighborhoods.
informal.HSDInteriorPointLP.HSDGeneratedAlgorithm: Proves that the generated even iterate satisfies the gap stopping test at the logarithmic pair bound.
Proves that the generated even iterate satisfies the duality-measure stopping test at the scaled logarithmic pair bound.
informal.HSDInteriorPointLP.HLP_newton_block_syst: Shows solvability of the Newton block system from the full-row-rank assumption through finite-dimensional linear algebra.
informal.HSDInteriorPointLP.YTM_contraction_power: Bounds the fixed YTM contraction power by the corresponding exponential decay estimate.

records.title: Gödel's First and Second Incompleteness Theorems
records.abstract: Formalizes Gödel's first and second incompleteness theorems for first-order arithmetic, building on formalized arithmetization and provability-logic infrastructure.

informal.LeanPool.Incompleteness.goedelFirst: Proves Gödel's first incompleteness theorem: a Sigma1-sound Delta1-definable theory extending arithmetic is incomplete.
informal.LeanPool.Incompleteness.goedelSecond: Proves Gödel's second incompleteness theorem: such a theory cannot prove its own consistency.

records.title: Infinitary logic and countable model theory
records.abstract: Formalizes the syntax and semantics of infinitary logic and a broad collection of its classical theorems: Scott sentences and ranks, Karp's theorem, model existence, the sharp Morley--Hanf bound, Craig, Lyndon, and Malitz interpolation, López--Escobar definability, undefinability of well-ordering, the Silver--Burgess and Morley counting dichotomies, and an honest coded-fragment interface whose HF compactness theorem is derived from first-order compactness.

informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottSentence: Every countable structure in a countable relational language has an associated infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottSentence_charac: A countable structure satisfies the Scott sentence of another countable structure exactly when the two structures are isomorphic.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottRank: The Scott rank of a countable structure is the supremum of its element ranks plus one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.scottRank_lt_omega1: The Scott rank of every countable structure in a countable relational language is a countable ordinal.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.karp_theorem_w: Two relational structures admit a nonempty potential isomorphism exactly when they agree on every infinitary sentence over every branching carrier in their shared universe.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.model_existence: Every countable set of infinitary sentences in an equality-respecting consistency property over a countable language has a countable model.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.morley_hanf: Beth omega-one is a Hanf bound for every infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.Lomega1omegaHanfNumb: The Hanf number of countable-conjunction infinitary logic is exactly beth omega-one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_small_model_o: A sentence with arbitrarily large models has, at every infinite cardinality, a model realizing only countably many complete types.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_complete_sent: Every infinitary-small model belongs to a complete infinitary subclass contained in any prescribed sentence it satisfies.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_complete_kCat: A categorical sentence with arbitrarily large models has a complete categorical refinement at the same infinite cardinality.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.craig_interpolation: Every sentence entailment has an interpolant using only the function and relation symbols shared by its two endpoints.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.craig_pcSeparation: Disjoint projective infinitary classes can be separated by a single infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lyndon_interpolation: Every sentence entailment has an interpolant whose positive and negative relation occurrences lie in the corresponding shared occurrence sets.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.malitz_interpolation: An entailment with universal consequent in a relational language has a universal interpolant over the shared vocabulary.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.exists_model_relPres: If a sentence has chains of every countable length, some model carries a relation-preserving map from the rationals.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrder_type_bound: The order types of all well-ordered models of one infinitary sentence are bounded below omega-one.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrdering_undefin: No single infinitary sentence defines exactly the well-orders.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lopezEscobar_iff: A class of coded countable structures is Borel and isomorphism-invariant exactly when it is the model class of one infinitary sentence.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.lopezEscobar_action_: The López--Escobar characterization equivalently uses invariance under the natural permutation action on coded structures.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.wellOrderClass_not_m: The class of coded well-orders is not a Borel set in the logic space.
informal.gandy_harrington_for_relation: A Borel equivalence relation on a Polish space with uncountably many classes has a continuous Cantor injection of pairwise inequivalent points.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.silverBurgessDichoto: A standard-Borel quotient has at most countably many classes or exactly continuum many classes.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.morley_counting: Assuming the Silver--Burgess dichotomy, the number of isomorphism classes of coded countable models of an infinitary sentence is at most aleph-one or exactly the continuum.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.iso_borel_of_bounded: Isomorphism among models of an infinitary sentence is Borel whenever their Scott heights have a common countable bound.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.FamilyPresentation: A coded-family presentation packages codes with their indexed decoding and a certificate for admissible infinitary formation.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.CodedFamily: A coded family packages a certified family code with an explicitly indexed decoding, made unique by the presentation's decoding law.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.AdmissibleFragment: An admissible fragment is closed under exactly the coded infinitary families certified by its presentation.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.hfFragment: The hereditarily finite fragment consists of the infinitary formulas whose syntax contains no infinitary connective.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.hfAdmissibleFragment: The hereditarily finite fragment forms an admissible coded fragment without assuming compactness data.
informal.FirstOrder.Language.finitaryFragment_com: Every finitely satisfiable theory contained in the first-order image fragment has a model.

records.title: Infinite counterexamples to Connes's rigidity conjecture
records.abstract: Constructs one finitely generated property-(T) ICC group and an infinite family of finitely generated property-(T) ICC groups that are pairwise nonisomorphic and are each nonisomorphic to the first group, while all of their tracial group von Neumann algebras are normally star-isomorphic. This unconditional infinite-family result is independent of the pooled conditional two-group Connes-rigidity formalization.

informal.ConnesRigidity.infiniteConnesRigidity: Registry-friendly alias of the exact canonical infinite-family Connes-rigidity counterexample theorem below.
informal.ConnesRigidity.exists_infinite_pairwise_: There exist a finitely generated property-(T) ICC group and an infinite sequence of finitely generated property-(T) ICC groups such that all their tracial group von Neumann algebras are normally star-isomorphic, although the sequence is pairwise nonisomorphic and none of its groups is isomorphic to the distinguished group.

classification.branch: operator algebras and geometric group theory

records.title: Verified canonical labelling of finite graphs
records.abstract: Implements an individualisation-refinement canonical-labelling algorithm in the style of nauty and proves that its canonical adjacency form is invariant under vertex relabelling and classifies finite graphs up to isomorphism. The imported core includes the executable search, refinement, orbit-pruning and backjumping machinery together with its equivariance, termination, soundness and optimality proofs.

informal.IsoGraph.Canon.canonAdj_eq_iff: Two Boolean adjacency functions on Fin n have equal canonical forms exactly when one is a relabelling of the other by a vertex permutation.
informal.IsoGraph.Canon.canonAdj_relabel: Relabelling a finite graph by any permutation leaves its canonical adjacency form unchanged.
informal.IsoGraph.Canon.exists_relabel_of_canonAd: Equality of canonical adjacency forms yields an explicit permutation relating the original adjacency functions.

records.title: Prekopa-Leindler, Brunn-Minkowski, and the isoperimetric inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Prekopa-Leindler inequality, Brunn-Minkowski inequality, and an isoperimetric inequality.

informal.isoperimetric_inequality: Proves the isoperimetric inequality derived from Brunn-Minkowski.

records.title: The transcendence of π
records.abstract: Formalizes a self-contained proof, following Niven's 1939 argument, that the real and complex number π is transcendental over the rationals.

informal.IsTranscendentalPi: Proves that the complex number π is transcendental over ℚ.
informal.IsTranscendentalPiReal: Proves that the real number π is transcendental over ℚ.
informal.isAlgebraic_I_mul_pi_of_isAlgebraic_pi: Shows that if π is algebraic over ℚ then so is iπ.
informal.exists_monic_rat_poly_aeval_Ipi_eq_zero: Produces a monic rational polynomial vanishing at iπ when iπ is algebraic.

records.title: The Jacobian of a Compact Riemann Surface
records.abstract: Constructs the Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface as the period-lattice quotient of the dual of holomorphic 1-forms, and proves the surrounding theory it needs: the genus as the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms, discreteness and full rank 2g of the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map and its injectivity in positive genus, functoriality (pushforward, pullback, degree, and the projection formula), Riemann-Roch, Serre duality via Laurent tails, the residue theorem, the Dolbeault-Cech comparison, and finite dimensionality of the first cohomology by a Schwartz/Montel argument. The headline no-hack guard is that the genus vanishes exactly when the surface is homeomorphic to the sphere.

informal.genus_eq_zero_iff_homeo: A compact connected Riemann surface has genus zero if and only if it is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere.
informal.Jacobian.ofCurve_inj: The Abel-Jacobi map of a compact Riemann surface of positive genus is injective: two points with the same image coincide.
informal.Jacobian.pushforward_pullback: For a non-constant holomorphic map between compact Riemann surfaces, the pushforward composed with the pullback on Jacobians is multiplication by the degree of the map.

records.title: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma and Quantized JL
records.abstract: Formalizes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma end to end — a Gaussian random projection preserves pairwise distances of a finite point set up to a (1 ± ε) factor, so a distortion-ε embedding of any m-point set exists once k is logarithmic in m — together with the quantized JL (QJL) one-bit sign sketch: unbiasedness of the asymmetric 1-bit estimator and its sub-Gaussian distortion bound.

informal.JL.johnson_lindenstrauss: The abstract probabilistic-method union bound — if the summed per-pair distortion-failure probability is below one, a distortion-preserving map exists.
informal.JL.johnson_lindenstrauss_pointset: The end-to-end Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma — a Gaussian random projection into k dimensions embeds any m-point set with (1 ± ε) distortion once k is logarithmic in m.
informal.JL.qjlEstimator_unbiased: The QJL asymmetric 1-bit estimator is unbiased for the normalized inner product between key and query.
informal.JL.qjlEstimator_concentration_exp: Sub-Gaussian distortion bound for the QJL 1-bit estimator: deviation at least ε has probability at most 2·exp(-m·ε²/(π·‖q‖²)).

records.title: Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.

informal.KahnKalai.covering_theorem: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.
informal.KahnKalai.park_pham: There is an absolute positive constant K such that every ℓ-bounded finite family with ℓ at least two satisfies p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ; the proof supplies K = 100000.

records.title: Halving the Kalton-Roberts upper bound
records.abstract: Formalizes the paper-style Boolean-algebra theorem that every approximately additive real-valued set function is uniformly close to a finitely additive signed measure, proving the certified Kalton-Roberts constant bound below 19.838.

informal.KaltonRoberts.KR_constant_lt: Proves the headline certified bound that the Kalton-Roberts constant is strictly less than 9919/500, i.e. 19.838.
informal.KaltonRoberts.KR_constant_le_C₂: Proves the exact rational upper bound C₂ = 694198146664396294486127753 / 34994834677886019996000000 for the Kalton-Roberts constant.
informal.KaltonRoberts.set_algebra_bound_C₂: States the paper-style set-algebra formulation, where every approximately additive function on a Boolean subalgebra of sets is within C₂ times the error of a finitely additive signed measure.

records.title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
records.abstract: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.

informal.KasamiCyclicAdditive.carlet_kasami_cycli: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).
In the normalized range 1 ≤ k < n, the same coefficient triple count is 2^(2n-3), assuming characteristic two, |K| = 2^n, coprimality, and distinct nonzero coefficients.
informal.KasamiCyclicAdditive.kasami_half_size: Under the normalized admissibility hypotheses, the image of the Kasami derivative has exactly half as many elements as the field.

records.title: Disproof of the Köthe conjecture (Krempa's matrix form)
records.abstract: Refutes Köthe's 1930 conjecture in Krempa's matrix form: there is a ring R (the unitization of a nil algebra of three weighted backward shifts over the algebraic closure of F_2) with a nil two-sided ideal I such that the matrix ideal M_2(I) contains a non-nilpotent matrix. The compared theorem is exactly the negation of the research-open statement `Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix` from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, in every universe. The supporting library proves a multiprojective common-zero theorem via the Segre cone, the Nullstellensatz and Krull's height theorem, a mask-mortality theorem for one-row matrix pencils, a diagonal construction of universal mortal sequences, and a linearization theorem reducing nilness of a three-generator algebra to nilness of its root-row pencils.

informal.Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general: It is not the case that for every ring R, every nil two-sided ideal I of R and every finite index type n, the matrix ideal M_n(I) of M_n(R) is nil. This is the negation of Krempa's matrix form of Köthe's conjecture, stated verbatim as in Formal Conjectures.
informal.KoetheCounterexample.counterexample: In every universe there is a ring R with a nil two-sided ideal I such that some 2 x 2 matrix with entries in I is not nilpotent.
informal.KoetheMultiProjective.exists_common_zero: Over an algebraically closed field, at most 2N polynomials that are multihomogeneous of a common positive degree in each of N blocks of three variables have a common zero with no block equal to zero.
informal.KoetheCounterexample.maskMortality: Over an algebraically closed field, every one-row matrix pencil and every periodic mask with more than half of its residues free admit a mask-compatible word of nonzero letters whose forward product is the zero matrix.
informal.KoetheCounterexample.exists_universalMor: Over a countable field satisfying mask mortality there is a sequence of nonzero letter triples such that every pencil has all its windows of some fixed positive length equal to zero.
informal.KoetheCounterexample.nil_of_all_pencils_: If every root-row pencil lifted along three elements of an algebra is nilpotent, then the non-unital subalgebra they generate is nil.

records.title: The Komlós and Beck–Fiala bounds with constant 36
records.abstract: Proves that finitely many real vectors of Euclidean norm at most one admit signs whose sum has every coordinate bounded by 36, and deduces the Beck–Fiala discrepancy bound 36 times the square root of the maximum vertex degree for finite hypergraphs. The Karingula–Lovett splitting argument is supported by reusable finite-distribution, total-variation, transport, convex-hull, and matrix-discrepancy infrastructure. The near-invariant distribution uses discrete squared tent weights, and real vectors are handled by coordinatewise truncation toward zero.

informal.Komlos.discrepancy_le_of_forall_sum_sq_l: For a real matrix with arbitrary finite row and column index types, if each column has sum of squared entries at most one, its minimum signed-column discrepancy is at most 36.
informal.Komlos.exists_isColouring_forall_abs_sum: Any finite family of vectors in a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space, each of norm at most one, admits signs in {-1, 1} whose signed sum has absolute value at most 36 in every coordinate.
informal.Hypergraph.exists_isColouring_forall_abs: If a hypergraph has finitely many vertices and each vertex belongs to at most t edges, there is a {-1, 1} colouring of all vertices whose sum on each edge has absolute value at most 36 times sqrt(t).
informal.Komlos.exists_isColouring_mean_add_sum_m: For a finitely supported probability distribution on any real module and n vectors, if translation by six times each vector has total variation distance at most one third, some signed sum added to the mean belongs to the convex hull of the distribution's support.
informal.Komlos.exists_nearInvariant: Every positive-denominator integer grid in finite-dimensional real coordinate space admits a finitely supported mean-zero probability distribution in [-6, 6]^d whose total variation distance under any grid translation of Euclidean norm at most one is at most one third.

records.title: A Conditional Sieve Criterion for Twin Primes via Krafft Geometry
records.abstract: Introduces an original conditional sieve criterion for the Twin Prime Conjecture. Using a centered modular alignment (termed the Krafft alignment), proves that if the Rayleigh-Ritz quotient over the orthogonal unit sphere satisfies muMin < 1, then a twin prime pair must exist in the corresponding interval.

informal.KrafftSieve.krafft_sieve_guarantee_with_: Proves that muMin n < 1 is a sufficient condition for the existence of a twin prime pair in the corresponding interval.
informal.KrafftSieve.mu_min_lt_one_implies_tpc: If there are infinitely many intervals where the optimal multidimensional weight achieves a ratio strictly less than 1, then there are infinitely many twin primes. This is a conditional reduction; the hypothesis muMin n < 1 is not established here for any n.

records.title: Finite-N Kuramoto Synchronization
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite-N Kuramoto model of coupled phase oscillators: the order parameter and its unit bound, the potential/force gradient identities, smoothness and local Lipschitz continuity of the vector field with ODE existence and uniqueness, Lyapunov descent along trajectories, pairwise and semicircle contraction estimates, Hebbian phase/weight dynamics, and full convergence to synchrony under all-to-all coupling from initial phases in an open semicircle.

informal.kuramotoR_norm_le_one: The Kuramoto order parameter has norm at most one for any phase configuration.
informal.weighted_lyapunov_descent: The weighted Kuramoto potential is non-increasing along the gradient flow, since the sum of force times potential-derivative over all oscillators is at most zero.
informal.allToAll_convergence_to_synchrony: Under all-to-all coupling with positive strength and initial phases in an open semicircle, the order parameter norm tends to one, i.e. the oscillators synchronize.

records.title: Kurosh and Schreier subgroup theorems via covering graphs
records.abstract: Proves the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products, with factors given by actual intersections with conjugates of the original factors and with the decomposition maps induced by their inclusions. The development constructs Bass–Serre trees, quotient graphs, graph-of-groups covers, path lifting, and normal forms. It also gives an explicit finite Schreier basis and classifies automorphisms of a finite regular Schreier action by its quotient group. The finite-graph basis infrastructure is reused from LeanPool.FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

informal.GraphCoveringTheory.KuroshStatement.kuro: Every subgroup H of an arbitrary indexed free product admits a free product decomposition into a free group and subgroups of H that are intersections with conjugates of the original factors. The isomorphism to H is induced by the actual subgroup inclusions and a homomorphism from the free factor.
informal.GraphCoveringTheory.Kurosh.kurosh_decomp: H is isomorphic to the free product of its nontrivial vertex stabilizers in the quotient Bass–Serre graph and the free group of that graph.
informal.GraphCoveringTheory.schreier_basis_finty: A finite-index subgroup H of a free group on any finite generator type of cardinality r has an explicit free basis of size d*r + 1 - d, where d is its index and subtraction is natural-number subtraction. This formulation also covers the empty generator type.
If the finite generator type is nonempty, the basis has the classical Schreier size 1 + d*(r - 1).
informal.GraphCoveringTheory.finiteIndexQuotientD: For a finite-index normal subgroup H of a group G, the automorphism group of the finite regular Schreier G-action is isomorphic to G/H by right translations. This is a theorem about the action, not a classification of general topological covers.
informal.GraphCoveringTheory.Kurosh.kurosh_subgro: A subgroup with trivial stabilizers at every vertex of its quotient Bass–Serre graph is a free group.

records.title: Finite witnesses and the width hierarchy for language generation
records.abstract: Characterizes generation in the limit for arbitrary families of infinite languages over any countably infinite universe by finite positive witnesses. Ordered-history generators admit a single set-driven normalization, chosen before the target language. The separation-width invariant takes every value 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1; generation is equivalent to width at most omega. Reusable infrastructure includes locking witnesses, positive separation, bounded diagonal capture over arbitrary universes, transport under equivalences, and finite-query normalization on natural numbers. The formalized scope is the semantic characterization and hierarchy, not the paper's additional density-one or Turing-computability results in Appendices D and E.

informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.Simplified.ordina: For any family H of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe, there exists one ordered-history generator that eventually outputs an unseen target element on every exact presentation of every target in H if and only if H admits a finite positive witness assignment whose nonempty active subfamilies always have infinite common intersection.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.Simplified.univer: Every ordered-history generator over a countably infinite universe has one set-driven normalization that locks on every infinite target on which the original generator succeeds on all exact presentations. The normalization is chosen before the target.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.ordinary_iff_widt: A family of infinite languages over a countably infinite universe is generatable in the limit exactly when its separation width is at most omega.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.full_range: Over every countably infinite universe, every value in WithTop (WithTop Nat), representing 0, 1, 2, ..., omega, omega+1, is the separation width of some family of infinite languages.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.bounded_capture: Over an arbitrary universe, every sequence of uniformly bounded finite sets has infinitely many terms contained in one set D such that D contains none of a prescribed countable list of infinite cores.
informal.GenLimit.FiniteWitness.executable_univer: The finite-search normalization on natural numbers locks on every infinite language on which the supplied generator eventually succeeds on every exact presentation. This is a semantic correctness theorem for the defined procedure, without a formal Turing-computability claim.

classification.branch: formal language theory and learning theory

records.title: On the paucity of lattice triangles
records.abstract: Formalizes an analytic lower bound used in the paucity theorem for lattice triangles.

informal.analyticEngine_lower_bound: Proves the analytic-engine lower bound underlying the lattice-triangle result.

records.title: Analysis of Boolean functions in Lean
records.abstract: Walsh-Fourier analysis on Boolean functions, including Arrow's theorem and BLR linearity testing.

informal.LeanPool.LeanBooleanfun.BooleanFun.BV.di: Arrow's theorem for two-candidate Boolean voting rules.

records.title: Formalizations of theorems related to model checking
records.abstract: Proves that every linear temporal logic formula has an equivalent finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton (via negation normal form, alternating Büchi automata, and the Miyano-Hayashi breakpoint construction), and that every linear-time property decomposes as the intersection of a safety property and a liveness property.

informal.LeanModelChecking.for_any_LTL_formula_ex: For any linear temporal logic formula there exists an equivalent finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton, i.e. one whose state type is finite, accepting the same language.
informal.LeanModelChecking.LTL: The syntax of linear temporal logic formulas over a set of atomic propositions.
informal.LeanModelChecking.NBW: A nondeterministic Büchi automaton over a given alphabet of letters.
informal.LeanModelChecking.ABW.toNBW.lang_eq: The Miyano-Hayashi breakpoint construction turns any alternating Büchi automaton over a finite state space into a nondeterministic Büchi automaton accepting the same language.
informal.SafetyLivenessDecomposition.safety_liven: Every linear-time property is the intersection of a safety property and a liveness property.

records.title: Polynomial ABC (Mason–Stothers) and its corollaries
records.abstract: Formalizes the Mason–Stothers theorem (the polynomial ABC theorem) and derives the polynomial Fermat's Last Theorem, the Fermat–Catalan inequality, Davenport's theorem, and a no-parametrization corollary.

informal.LeanPolyABC.Polynomial.abc: Mason–Stothers — for coprime non-constant polynomials with a+b=c, the max degree is below the degree of the radical of abc.
informal.LeanPolyABC.Polynomial.flt: The polynomial Fermat's Last Theorem — no nontrivial coprime polynomial solutions of aⁿ+bⁿ=cⁿ for n ≥ 3.
informal.LeanPolyABC.Polynomial.flt_catalan: The polynomial Fermat–Catalan inequality bounding solutions of aᵖ+bᵍ=cʳ.

records.title: Lean-QuantumAlg
records.abstract: Provides a Mathlib-based library of formally verified quantum-algorithm definitions, primitives, and endpoints, including QFT, QSP, quantum kernels, amplitude amplification, Grover search, phase estimation, order finding, teleportation, and a Lie-algebraic barren-plateau witness.

informal.QuantumAlg.QuantumFourierTransform.main: Proves the QFT action on computational-basis states and records exact circuit counts.
informal.QuantumAlg.ReflectionBasedQuantumSignalP: Characterizes reflection-based single-qubit QSP transforms in the Chebyshev basis.
informal.QuantumAlg.TrigonometricQuantumSignalPro: Characterizes trigonometric single-qubit QSP transforms in the YZZYZ form.
informal.QuantumAlg.QuantumKernel.main: Proves that fidelity quantum-kernel Gram matrices are positive semidefinite.
informal.QuantumAlg.QuantumKernelAdvantage.separa: States the conditional quantum-kernel learning separation from discrete-log hardness.
informal.QuantumAlg.fullControllability_hasBarren: Exhibits an exponentially vanishing loss-variance family for a fully controllable dynamical Lie algebra, conditional on the assumed Ragone second-moment variance law (the Haar/Weingarten averaging identity Var = P_g(rho)*P_g(O)/dim, taken as a hypothesis rather than derived from a circuit twirl).
informal.QuantumAlg.GroverSearch.main_success_pro: Derives Grover search success probability from the amplitude-amplification closed form.

records.title: Craig Interpolation for Gödel-Löb logic via coalgebraic proofs
records.abstract: Formalizes a proof-theoretic Craig interpolation theorem for Gödel-Löb provability logic, built on a coalgebraic notion of circular proof.

informal.Lean4GlCoalgebras.interpolation: Proves the Craig interpolation theorem for Gödel-Löb provability logic.

records.title: Coinductive Interaction Trees using QPFs
records.abstract: Formalizes coinductive interaction trees as the M-type of a polynomial functor (via Mathlib QPFs), proving the lawful functor and monad structure, a bisimulation equality coinciding with propositional equality, and iteration and effect-handler interpretation combinators, supported by a vendored parameterized-coinduction (Paco) library.

informal.Lean4Itree.ITree: Defines the coinductive interaction tree as the final coalgebra (M-type) of the interaction-tree polynomial functor.
informal.Lean4Itree.ITree.IEq: Defines bisimulation equality between interaction trees as a coinductive fixed point.
informal.Lean4Itree.ITree.ieq_iff_eq: Proves that bisimulation equality of interaction trees coincides with propositional equality.
informal.Lean4Itree.ITree.bind_assoc: Proves associativity of monadic bind for interaction trees, part of the LawfulMonad instance.
informal.Lean4Itree.ITree.iter: Defines the iteration combinator producing an interaction tree from a step function.
informal.Lean4Itree.ITree.interp: Defines interpretation of an interaction tree against an effect handler into an arbitrary iterable monad.
informal.Lean4Itree.plfp_acc: Proves the accumulation principle for the parameterized least fixed point underlying the Paco coinduction library.

records.title: Formalized Complex Analysis in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes Poisson integral formulas on the unit disc and arbitrary centered discs, Herglotz–Riesz representation, and Harnack's inequality on the unit disc, plus infrastructure for univalent function classes S and Σ.

informal.LeanPool.LeanComplexAnalysis.poisson_int: Proves the Poisson integral formula for harmonic functions on the unit disc.
Proves the Poisson integral formula for harmonic functions on arbitrary centered discs.
informal.LeanPool.LeanComplexAnalysis.HerglotzRie: Proves that every positive harmonic function on the unit disc with value 1 at 0 has a unique Herglotz–Riesz representation by a probability measure on the unit circle.
informal.LeanPool.LeanComplexAnalysis.harnack_ine: Proves Harnack's inequality for positive harmonic functions on the unit disc.

records.title: Modular forms and the generalized residue theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Hungerbühler-Wasem generalized residue theorem for Cauchy principal value integrals through poles and applies it to the valence formula for modular forms on the modular group.

informal.generalizedResidueTheorem: Proves the Hungerbühler-Wasem generalized residue theorem for piecewise-C1 curves through poles.
informal.generalizedResidueTheorem_simplePoles: Specializes the generalized residue theorem to the simple-pole case.
informal.valence_formula_textbook_orbit_finsum: Proves the valence formula for modular forms on the modular group.

records.title: Lehmer's Polynomial and the E10 Coxeter Element
records.abstract: Proves that Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial — the integer polynomial of smallest known Mahler measure above 1 — is irreducible over the integers, and that it is the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group (the rank-10 instance of McMullen). Against Mathlib's Mahler-measure API it computes M(L) exactly as the Salem root with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5, states Lehmer's conjecture as a defined Prop (never assumed) with the strong form implying the gap form, and contrasts the E8 Coxeter element (order exactly 30) with the E10 element (infinite order in GL(10,Z)): the E-series crosses from torsion to a Salem matrix at rank 10, and the crossing value is Lehmer's number.

informal.LehmerE10.main_theorem: Lehmer's polynomial L(x) = x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 is irreducible over the integers, and the characteristic polynomial of a Coxeter element of the E10 Weyl group equals L.
informal.LehmerE10.lehmer_mahlerMeasure: The Mahler measure of L equals its Salem root mu, with the unconditional bounds 1 < M(L) < 7/5.

records.title: Lentil: Temporal Logic of Actions in Lean 4
records.abstract: A shallow embedding of Leslie Lamport's Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA) in Lean 4, with the temporal modalities, standard propositional and temporal proof rules, weak-fairness and leads-to reasoning, and an interactive proof mode for TLA judgments.

informal.TLA.always: Defines the TLA "always" (box) temporal modality, asserting a predicate holds on every suffix of an execution.
informal.TLA.eventually: Defines the TLA "eventually" (diamond) temporal modality, asserting a predicate holds on some suffix of an execution.
informal.TLA.always_induction: The always-induction rule, equating `□ p` with `p` together with `□ (p → ◯ p)`.
informal.TLA.wf1: The WF1 weak-fairness proof rule deriving a leads-to property from a next-state action under weak fairness.
informal.TLA.wf_as_leads_to: Characterizes weak fairness of an action as a leads-to property between its enabledness and its occurrence.

records.title: Foundational local complex-analytic geometry
records.abstract: Develops a common Lean foundation for several classical local theorems in several complex variables: complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation with full germ uniqueness, Noetherianity of holomorphic-germ rings, finite projection for hypersurface germs, the holomorphic constant-rank normal form, and the finite-family local analytic Nullstellensatz. The imported development also exposes the arbitrary-ideal Nullstellensatz and regular level-set, submersion, and immersion consequences.

informal.LocalComplexGeometry.localAnalyticNullst: If a finite family of functions analytic at the origin has common zero set locally contained in the zero set of another analytic function, then a positive power of the latter is locally an analytic linear combination of the family.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphicGerm_isN: For every finite complex dimension, including dimension zero, the local ring of holomorphic germs at the origin is Noetherian.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.hypersurface_finite: A nonzero hypersurface germ vanishing at the origin admits a linear coordinate change whose local quotient is finite free over the base germ ring, together with an explicit prepared equation and a proper, surjective finite-fiber projection of the local zero set.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphic_constan: An analytic map of locally constant complex rank is locally equivalent, through analytic source and target coordinates, to the standard rank projection.
informal.ClassicalComplexWPT.classicalComplexWeie: A complex-analytic germ of exact order in one distinguished variable factors uniquely into a nonvanishing analytic unit and a monic Weierstrass polynomial whose analytic coefficient germs vanish at the origin.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.analyticNullstellen: For every ideal of the local holomorphic-germ ring, the ideal of germs vanishing on its local zero set equals its radical.
informal.LocalComplexGeometry.holomorphic_regular: Near a regular point, the level set of a holomorphic map admits an analytic parametrization with an analytic local inverse on the level set.

classification.branch: several complex variables and local analytic geometry

records.title: Improved long gaps between consecutive primes
records.abstract: Formalizes the unconditional lower bound showing that, for all sufficiently large X, the largest gap between consecutive primes below X is at least a positive constant times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2. The development includes the short-translates sieve proposition, divisor coefficient estimates, truncated product weights, moment bounds, and the Erdos--Rankin covering argument used to derive the headline result.

informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_prime_gaps: There are a positive constant c and a real threshold X0 such that for every X at least X0, some pair of consecutive indexed primes below X has gap greater than c times log X (log log X)^2 log log log log X / (log log log X)^2.
informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.long_gap_theorem: For all sufficiently large X, there are consecutive primes p < q with q at most X and q - p at least a fixed positive multiple of the improved long-gap scale.
informal.LongGapsBetweenPrimes.short_translates: For all sufficiently large x, every sufficiently sparse subset S of an interval of length between x and x(log x)^2 has a translate b + Q(x)t + S consisting entirely of composite numbers, with 1 <= t <= exp x.

records.title: Classification of low-dimensional solvable Lie algebras
records.abstract: Formalises the classification of solvable Lie algebras up to dimension three.

informal.LieAlgebra.Dim3.classification: Classifies three-dimensional solvable Lie algebras over arbitrary fields.

records.title: The main theorem of polytopes
records.abstract: Formalizes the Minkowski–Weyl theorem — the equivalence between V-polytopes (convex hulls of finite point sets) and bounded H-polytopes (finite intersections of half-spaces) in a finite-dimensional real vector space.

informal.MainTheoremOfPolytopes: The Minkowski–Weyl theorem — a set is a V-polytope iff it is a bounded H-polytope.
informal.Vpolytope_of_Hpolytope: Every bounded H-polytope (finite intersection of half-spaces) is the convex hull of a finite point set.

records.title: Global completeness of one-sorted definedness-free matching logic
records.abstract: Formalizes the one-sorted case of Chen and Roșu's global-completeness argument and independently discharges its local-completeness oracle by mechanizing the canonical-model construction from their 2019 Matching μ-Logic technical report (Theorem 73, Lemmas 80–81, and strong local completeness Theorem 83). The resulting theorem supplies both local completeness and soundness for countably infinite variable types.

informal.MatchingLogic.locality: For a backward-closed subset of a matching-logic model, two valuations that agree inside the subset and both stay outside it otherwise give identical denotations after restriction to that subset.
informal.MatchingLogic.two_copies: The double-cover model over a nonempty backward-closed proper subset has exactly the denotation predicted by each of its two projections back to the original model.
informal.MatchingLogic.semantic_localization: For a closed theory and closed conclusion, global semantic consequence is equivalent to local consequence from the localized theory.
informal.MatchingLogic.strongLocalCompleteness: One-sorted basic matching logic has strong local completeness over an arbitrary one-sorted finitary signature when the element-variable type is countably infinite.
informal.MatchingLogic.global_completeness_entryI: For a one-sorted finitary signature, closed premises and conclusion, and a countably infinite element-variable type, global semantic consequence is equivalent to derivability, with both soundness and local completeness discharged.

records.title: Improved asymptotic bounds for binary and spherical codes
records.abstract: Formalizes asymptotic coding bounds obtained from multilevel harmonic analysis, branching rules, and spectral decompositions. The development proves a binary-code exponent strictly below the MRRW rate, constructs a strict hierarchy of spherical-code bounds, and derives the published 0.39661 asymptotic kissing-number exponent. This import incorporates substantial proof and performance optimizations by Dean Cureton.

informal.MetricCodes.Johnson.main_binary_theorem: For every relative distance strictly between zero and one half, the combined variational upper bound on the asymptotic binary-code rate is valid and is strictly smaller than the MRRW rate.
informal.MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.ma: Every feasible finite interlacing certificate gives an eventual exponential upper bound for spherical codes, while the spherical-code rate is bounded by the closed hierarchy's variational rate.
informal.MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.st: At every angle parameter strictly between zero and one, successive levels of both the global and localized hierarchies improve strictly, with the localized hierarchy also strictly improving the row and classical bounds.
informal.MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.Nu: In all sufficiently large dimensions, the kissing number is at most 2 raised to 0.39661 times the dimension.

records.title: Minimum modulus for the unique multiset-sum problem
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact minimum modulus `N_min(n) = 2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}` for the unique multiset-sum problem on the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}`, and proves the sharp elementary-abelian-2-group lower bound `k >= n - 1` for unique multiset sums in `(Z/2Z)^k`.

informal.MinModulus.nmin_eq: Proves that among moduli `N >= 2` the least one making the super-increasing residue set `{2^i - 1 : 0 <= i < n}` valid for the unique multiset-sum problem is `2^n - 2^{floor(log_2 n)}`, for every `n >= 2` (stated as `IsLeast`).
informal.MinModulus.elementaryAbelianTwoGroups_op: Proves that if `g_0, ..., g_{n-1}` in `(Z/2Z)^k` have unique multiset sums, then `k >= n - 1`: an elementary abelian 2-group admitting such a family has order at least `2^(n - 1)`.

records.title: BKLO simultaneous perfect matchings and spread matchings
records.abstract: Formalizes the r = 2 specialization of the simultaneous factor-selection step in BKLO Lemma 10.7: under quantitative parity, minimum-degree, codegree, and incidence hypotheses, a linearly sized, overlapping family of neighbourhood graphs admits perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof replaces the published randomized greedy process by a deterministic pessimistic-estimator sweep. Supporting results develop perfect, near-perfect, edge-disjoint, and quantitatively weighted spread matchings from sharp minimum-degree hypotheses.

informal.BKLOK2.lemma107K2_holds: Specializes BKLO Lemma 10.7 to r = 2 in its apex-neighbourhood configuration: for every sufficiently large admissible configuration, all indexed neighbourhood graphs admit perfect matchings whose edge sets are pairwise disjoint. The proof is deterministic.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_isPerfectMatching_of_: Every finite simple graph of even order whose minimum degree is at least half its order has a perfect matching.
informal.SimpleGraph.exists_isMatching_compl_sing: Every finite simple graph of odd order n and minimum degree at least (n - 1) / 2 has a matching whose vertex set is the complement of a singleton.
