records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: elliotglazer/erdos501
records.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

records.title: rwst/Even-Integral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery and the formalization are the AI agent's; the agent also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the agent is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A kernel-checked certificate for the finite mathematical core of the paper's explicit 16-vertex counterexample. The compared declarations prove cubicity, bipartiteness, connectivity after every deletion of at most two vertices, Hamiltonicity of the displayed cycle, its exact complementary perfect matching, the displayed oriented facial incidence and dual data, Euler's equality, properness and uniqueness up to global permutation of the face coloring, the induced edge-color classes, their unavoidable intersections with the complementary matching, and the instantiated final obstruction. The topological realization of the incidence data as a sphere embedding and the published algorithm's Property 1 remain external inputs.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the paper's standard finite-word semantics for k-uniform two-word π-representability, its neighbourhood-trace bound binomial(k(|A|+1),k)^2, the explicit 20-by-741322 bit-incidence graph B20, and the theorem that B20 is not representable by two 2-uniform words. It also retains the companion's token-order bridge and exact arithmetic endpoints.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: Lean formalization of the paper's finite skew-symmetric path instance, exact prefix-deletion completion oracle, deterministic oracle-pruned DFS, correctness and duplicate-freedom, and an executable DFS event trace whose extracted first-output, inter-output, post-output, and no-output work intervals satisfy the paper-level depth/LCP bounds.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Lemma 7.1 and the outer-matrix content of Theorem 7.2 for generalized cubic subdivision. It defines the naturally indexed 28n by 28n outer matrix row-by-row from the authenticated released MATLAB masks, including all previous/current/next-sector references. It constructs the paper's explicit topological permutation, proves that the first 24n coordinates are strictly upper triangular and that the remaining diagonal components are n scalar 1/64 blocks and n copies of the displayed 3 by 3 core, and proves unconditionally for every n at least 3 the characteristic polynomial X^(24n)(X-1/64)^n(X-1/32)^n(X-1/16)^n(X-1/8)^n.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A concrete formalization of the infinite-family construction in the source: cycle and Cartesian-product distances on P_m □ C_(6m), the displayed landmarks (0,0), (0,2m), and (m-1,0), the four-piece cycle distance-pair locus, and injectivity of the resulting unordered multiset code for every even m at least 2. This establishes the three-landmark resolving upper bound. It does not formalize the separate general lower bound needed to conclude that the set is a basis or that the multiset dimension equals 3.

records.title: rwst/Square-Roots
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 3 asks whether √3 lies in 𝒮 or in 𝒵. This formalization settles that question and the whole square-root slice: √3 ∈ 𝒵 by an explicit ξ = 1.34160899796…, and for an integer m ≥ 2 one has √m ∈ 𝒮 exactly when m = 2. The cells √5, √6, √7, √8 put four explicit points of 𝒵 in the interval (2,3), the only interval where an answer to Dubickas's Problem 5 could live; they are formalized (SZ.exists_mem_MahlerZ_Ioo_two_three) but are not separately compared, being subsumed by the compared Theorem B. The mechanism is not Diophantine approximation but the arithmetic of Cantor sets, and rests on the triviality that √m² = m is an integer: splitting n into even and odd values turns the one orbit into two base-m orbits coupled by x + √m y = σ, and a covering induction — Utz's 1951 theorem on the distance set of the Cantor discontinuum at m = 3, proved here for every base and every modulus — solves that equation inside the restricted-digit set. The same machinery at a general modulus gives, for p ≥ 2 and non-square m ≥ 3 in either of two explicit ranges, a real ξ ≠ 0 with p ∣ ⌊ξ√mⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 1, hence integral parts that are composite from some point on; and the greedy's branching shows the witnesses for √3 have cardinality 2^ℵ₀, so all but countably many of them are transcendental. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.32215.43682. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery is the Fable-5 agent's; the formalization is the Fable-5 and Opus-5 agents'; the agents also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the collaboration is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency of the development itself.

records.title: rwst/Confinement-Certificates
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper on the emptiness theory of the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, at and beyond the window length 1/p. The paper introduces block certificates --- finite integer witnesses, rechecked from scratch by the Lean proof kernel, whose soundness rests on the aperiodicity lemma alone --- and uses them to pass the length-$1/p$ line: $\Zset_{3/2}(1/6,13/24)=\emptyset$ (window length $3/8>1/3$), $\Zset_{3/2}(961/3600,2427/3600)=\emptyset$ (length $733/1800$), and explicit unions of total length up to $17/24$, against $20/39$ in print. The closed-interval union statement of Dubickas is replicated exactly as printed; no $\xi\ne0$ keeps $\|\xi(3/2)^{n}\|<1/5$ for every $n$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the distance to the nearest integer; and thirty windows of length $1/p$ are certified at five bases in the regime $p>q^{2}$ that Dubickas leaves open. There is no sorry anywhere outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and no native_decide: every block certificate is discharged by `c.ok = true := by decide`, i.e. by kernel reduction of integer arithmetic on the certificate's raw data.

records.title: Three Sharp Bounds for Hansen Polytopes of Cographs
records.abstract: A Lean 4/Mathlib formalisation of three sharp lower bounds for Hansen polytopes of finite nonempty cographs: normalized Mahler volume at least one, at least 3^d nonempty faces, and at least 2^d d! full flags in dimension d. In each result equality holds exactly for threshold graphs.

records.title: JaTaSn/lattice-line-covers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22550: there is a family of lattice lines covering the integer plane whose set of realized directions is dense. Concretely, a family F of subsets of Z^2 is exhibited such that (i) every member is a genuine lattice line, the nonempty solution set of Px + Qy = c with P, Q coprime; (ii) the members cover Z^2; (iii) two members of different direction are disjoint, so no lattice point is covered twice in different directions; and (iv) the directions that occur are dense in the space RP^1 of line directions, that is, every angle in [0, pi) is approximated to within any epsilon by the direction of some member. The construction is recursive and works on nested regions: a chain of cosets Z^2 = R_0 > R_1 > R_2 > ... is built, and at stage k the region R_k is partitioned into sub-cosets of a new coprime direction, one of which is reserved to become R_{k+1} while lines of that direction claim all the others. Coverage is what the choice of reserved sub-coset is for: fix a surjective enumeration z_0, z_1, ... of Z^2 and reserve, at stage k, a sub-coset that does not contain z_k -- always possible, since the partition has at least four sub-cosets and only the one containing z_k must be avoided. Every point is then claimed: it is z_k for some k, and either it had already left the region at an earlier stage, in which case the coverage invariant Z^2 \ R_k = union over i < k of (R_i \ R_{i+1}) shows it was claimed there, or it is still in R_k and the reservation rule places it in a sub-coset claimed at stage k. Reserving an arbitrary sub-coset would not do: without that diagonal choice a point could survive in every R_k and never be claimed. Disjointness is a consequence of that partition rather than of any criterion for when two individual lines meet: distinct sub-cosets of a region are disjoint, each stage's lines stay inside the sub-cosets they claim, and the regions claimed at distinct stages are therefore disjoint. Earlier lines survive untouched because everything a later stage touches lies inside the reserved region. Only Theorem 1 is formalized; the paper's further remarks and discussion are not.

records.title: Polylogarithmic Descent for Almost All Collatz Orbits in Natural Density
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four strengthened almost-all results for shortcut and raw Collatz orbits in ordinary natural density: critical polylogarithmic descent with arbitrary positive divergent target and height multipliers, centered trajectory tubes, and actual first-passage clocks; the fixed-exponent common-landing theorem with the exact upper exceptional-rate endpoint; an explicit reciprocal-order lower bound forced by the joint height ceiling; and a quantitative stretched-logarithmic common-landing theorem with smaller relative-height ceilings. These are almost-all statements and do not prove pointwise Collatz convergence.

records.title: BSCAveraging
records.abstract:
Three theorems about binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source: a pair (𝑋, 𝑌) of
Bernoulli(1/2) bits with P(𝑋 ≠ 𝑌) = 𝑝, together with Markov chains 𝑈 - 𝑋 - 𝑌 - 𝑉 in which 𝑈
and 𝑉 are the outputs of two independent binary channels applied to 𝑋 and to 𝑌. Let 𝒜 be the
set of rate triples (𝑅₀, 𝑅₁, 𝑅₂) with 𝐼(𝑈;𝑋) ≤ 𝑅₁, 𝐼(𝑌;𝑉) ≤ 𝑅₂ and 𝑅₀ ≤ 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and ℬ the same set with both channels restricted
to be binary symmetric.

(1) conv 𝒜 = conv ℬ for every 𝑝 in [0,1]. (2) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose rates
do not exceed those of the Z-channel with parameter 𝑎 and the S-channel with parameter 𝑑
attains a larger 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉) than that pair does. (3) At 𝑝 = 0, no pair of binary channels whose
rates are at least those of the Z-channels with parameters 𝑎 and 𝑑 attains a smaller 𝐼(𝑈;𝑉)
than that pair does. Here 𝑎, 𝑑 range over (0,1).

records.title: Vulkin-prog/paper-c-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of global and finite-prefix Poisson laws for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function, corresponding to Theorem 16.2 and Corollary 16.4 of the cited source article. The selected declarations give the global interior start-count law on a finite prime-sign cylinder, its recentering at M/2^L, the corresponding theorem on the infinite Rademacher product, and the finite-prefix start-count and longest-stretch law. All asymptotics are uniform in the critical window |L - log_2 M| <= C. Each declaration is conditional on exactly six fully stated ordinary source propositions; those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.title: nielstron/langlib
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of grammar and automaton presentations of the extended Chomsky hierarchy. Starting from unrestricted-grammar rewriting, it defines regular, linear, context-free, context-sensitive, indexed, deterministic context-free, recursive, and recursively enumerable language classes; relates finite, pushdown, linearly bounded, and Mathlib TM0 automata to the corresponding grammar classes; proves strict hierarchy inclusions; and establishes closure or non-closure under thirteen operations for seven major classes.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/jacobian-conjecture-lean
records.abstract: An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the explicit three-dimensional polynomial map announced by Levent Alpöge in 2026. The project proves that its formal Jacobian determinant is the nonzero constant -2, verifies an explicit three-point fibre over the complex numbers, and derives the failure of injectivity required to refute the dimension-three Jacobian conjecture. The source formulas and proof scope are recorded explicitly; no claim is made about the still-open two-dimensional case.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the general n-dimensional combinatorial Sperner parity theorem on abstract n-dimensional pseudomanifolds with boundary for arbitrary dimension n : ℕ. Proves the local door-counting parity invariant on (n+1)-simplices, the global double-counting identity on door-facet incidences, and the master parity congruence modulo 2 relating panchromatic (n+1)-simplices to boundary doors. The theorem is conditional on an odd number of boundary (n-1)-doors; obtaining the classical geometric Sperner lemma for simplicial subdivisions of geometric simplices with boundary-preserving colorings is a specialization requiring an additional geometric boundary induction argument not contained in these abstract combinatorial declarations. This n-dimensional development (SpernerND.lean) generalizes and supersedes the fixed-dimensional combinatorial parity identities in the repository's lower-dimensional modules (SpernersLemma.lean and Sperner3D.lean) into a single unified parameterized architecture. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/HigherLambdaModel
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of higher-dimensional structure in the untyped lambda calculus.  Arthur Ramos is the first author and responsible maintainer of the Lean formalization; Daniel O. Martinez-Rivillas and Ruy J.G.B. de Queiroz are credited as the mathematical/source authors whose results are formalized.  The Palomar surface uses a restricted Kan-complex exponential and a separate certificate for term-generated semantic bodies, while the substantive repository also formalizes the higher conversion tower and the concrete K-infinity homotopy lambda model.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/SpinorLean
records.abstract: Formalizes an exterior-model spinor construction for a field K in which 2 is invertible, using an explicit hyperbolic presentation and the Clifford conjugation action on the ambient quadratic space.  The development proves field-sensitive covering and image results: the positive split-rank spin-to-isometry kernel is {1,-1}, the spin action therefore descends only projectively, the split-line image is exactly the square-scaling subgroup, and a finite-dimensional split Levi element associated to g lies in the ambient spin image exactly when det(g) is a square unit.  The repository also packages the chosen exterior model, half-spin pieces, explicit transvection and square-scaling Clifford lifts, square-class quotient characters, vector-product norm identities, and selected complex and real low-dimensional Clifford classifications.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Refined Arbitrary-Target Transport Through Collatz Endpoints
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative stability theorem for the one-block endpoint-pullback operator of the shortcut Collatz map. If an arbitrary target set has at most C N^(1-D) exceptions among the positive integers up to N, then, for every central Renyi order 1/2 < theta < 1, every admissible fixed central window, and every positive transport coefficient below the explicit asymptotic slope, its pullback through one floor(log_2 n)-step endpoint is (K(1+C^(theta/(1+theta)))D^(-theta/(2(1+theta))), transport*D)-dense whenever D is sufficiently small. The cutoff and K depend only on the fixed moment and transport parameters, not on the target set or C,D.

records.title: yuhangshi888/sun-cotangent-permanent-counterexample-lean
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the exact evaluation of the normalized 14 by 14 cotangent permanent at p = 29. The formalization proves that its value is 84643985981440 and hence gives a counterexample to the cotangent sign inequality in Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 4.7(ii). It includes the analytic-to-cyclotomic bridge, two separately kernel-checked finite permanent certificates, Chinese-remainder and coefficientwise integer lifting, the Section 3 Archimedean uniqueness argument, and equation (4.1) in the integral cyclotomic quotient.

records.title: BrandonMYates/schwarzschild-comparator
records.abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.

records.title: yuningyang19/parameter_free_gradient_p
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of three results about exact value-gradient oracle complexity in finite-dimensional l_p geometry: strict-local scale-identification impossibility at fixed LR/epsilon = 4, the known-parameter p > 2 upper/lower exponent p/(p+2) with its stated horizon and dimension qualifications, and a post-secant-initialization parameter-free runtime family with the three p regimes. The Comparator surface contains exactly these three declarations; the other certified results remain supporting proof infrastructure.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/NagataFactoriality
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Nagata's factoriality theorem for noetherian integral domains.  It proves that unique factorization descends from a localization when every denominator is a finite product of prime elements, packages the specialization to submonoids generated by sets of primes, and demonstrates the method with a Nagata-based polynomial UFD theorem.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract: The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}), constructed from the multiplication rather than assumed: symmetric, associative, and positive definite. Symmetry and associativity need neither finite dimensionality nor formal reality; positive definiteness needs both, and runs through the spectral theorem. The carrier is not assumed unital, so this supplies the Euclidean form itself and does not by itself establish a unital Euclidean Jordan algebra. Sits directly on Mathlib's IsCommJordan. Coordinatization is absent. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the source-facing polynomial-cube exclusion at actual partial degrees (6,9).  From literal bivariate polynomials of outer degrees six and nine, leading coefficients s^6 and s^9 for a common polynomial s, and nonzero constant Keller bracket, the formalization proves that no such source exists, including when s is constant.  It constructs the finite-pole or infinity expansion, exhausts every timing of the eight Faber loads through rho2, and excludes the remaining elliptic, cusp, zero-invariant, and constant-core terminal fibres.  It does not claim the reduction from an arbitrary Keller pair, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or the plane Jacobian conjecture.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/dinitz-garg-goemans-counterexample-lean
records.abstract: A standalone Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the finite counterexample to the cost-preserving single-source unsplittable-flow conjecture. The development realizes a directed graph with seven vertices, nine arcs, and three terminal demands; checks a feasible rational fractional flow of cost 58 with maximum demand 15; and proves that every unsplittable routing under the weak additive congestion bound has cost at least 60. It also derives the failure of the strict congestion variant. No general algorithmic or complexity-theoretic claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: yuhangshi888/zeta-simple-zeros-673316977
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the supporting-plane and exact-arithmetic portion of the finite-dimensional argument in Yuhang Shi's research draft on simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function. It proves a conditional scalar two-certificate supporting-plane implication, its explicit piecewise-square-root specialization at block length 219, and the exact strict comparison above 673316977/10^9 for the resulting local assembly expression. The spectral derivation of the trace-envelope alternative, the upstream seven- and nine-point interval certificates, and the analytic passage from finite blocks to a global zeta-zero proportion are not formalized here and are not claimed as Palomar-verified conclusions.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/TopologicalComputationalPaths
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of topological semantics for endpoint-varying computational paths.  It constructs both the canonical final composable quotient and the ordinary pullback of quotient arrows.  The selected result proves that the canonical comparison is a continuous bijection and characterizes exactly when it is quotient, a homeomorphism, and an induced topology agreement; under these equivalent conditions ordinary composition is continuous.  It also records discontinuity as an obstruction and proves compact--Hausdorff and discrete sufficient cases.  The selected certificate additionally requires full additive classifications of the genuine based-loop spaces `AddCircle (1 : ℝ)` by `ℤ` and its product torus by `ℤ × ℤ`: the invariant, identity value, composition additivity, explicit standard representatives, and both inverse laws are checked using covering-map lifts and coordinatewise arguments.  It also formalizes the observable based fiber of the universal continuous-path presentation, its homeomorphism to the standard based loop quotient, the final/ordinary pair comparison, and the source-backed Hawaiian-earring transfer: the non-quotient square and discontinuous multiplication force failure of the scoped ordinary-pair quotient, topology agreement, and ordinary multiplication continuity under the comparison.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: nimaanari/formalization-beyond-bethe
records.abstract: Computing or approximating the permanent is a canonical problem in theoretical computer science and in counting and sampling.  Before this work, the canonical Bethe approximation gave the best known deterministic guarantee, with approximation factor (sqrt 2)^n.  This formalization proves that there is an absolute constant c < sqrt 2 and a deterministic polynomial-time c^n-approximation for every nonnegative rational matrix. It checks the mathematical and algorithmic proof down to Lean's standard logical axioms, including the finite-precision convex-optimization implementation.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Radon's Lemma (Johann Radon, 1921) and Helly's Theorem on intersecting families of convex sets (Eduard Helly, 1923; Freek Wiedijk #99) from first principles. Proves that any d + 2 points in ℝ^d admit a Radon partition into two disjoint subsets whose convex hulls intersect, and uses Radon's lemma by induction on the family size to prove Helly's theorem for finite families of convex sets under the general <= d + 1 subfamily intersection hypothesis (covering small families |ι| <= d + 1 as well as large families). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract: The frame Peirce decomposition: relative to a Jordan frame, a Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs of frame indices, and in finite dimension the diagonal blocks are lines, dim V_ii = 1 - the Faraut-Koranyi table entry. The frame is carried as data, so frame conjugacy is sidestepped and nothing here claims anything about the rank of J. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/hadamard-668-lean
records.abstract: An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a supplied bordered block-circulant sign matrix of order 668.  The main theorem proves that there exists a 668 by 668 integer matrix with entries in {-1, 1}, diagonal row norm 668, and zero inner product between every pair of distinct rows. The formalization is a certificate-specific existence result, not a classification of Hadamard matrices and not a proof of the general Hadamard conjecture.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: BochaoKong/classical-complex-wpt
records.abstract: A Mathlib-only Lean 4 formalization of the classical complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation theorem at the origin. For every number of base variables and every preparation degree, including the zero-dimensional and degree-zero cases, it constructs the distinguished monic polynomial and nonvanishing analytic unit and proves uniqueness of all factors as germs.

records.title: mccorvie/classification-of-surfaces
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the classification theorem for compact connected topological 2-manifolds, including surfaces with boundary. The main theorem proves that every compact connected Hausdorff 2-manifold modeled on the Euclidean half-plane is homeomorphic to the sphere, an orientable canonical quotient surface, or a non-orientable canonical quotient surface. The submitted theorem is the exact statement of the Lean Eval `topological_classification_of_surfaces` challenge.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Bárány's Colorful Carathéodory Theorem (1982), Bárány's First Selection Lemma (1982), the 1D Centerpoint Theorem, and geometric deductions from first principles. Proves that for any d + 1 sets of points S_0, ..., S_d in R^d whose convex hulls all contain a common target point p, there exists a colorful transversal f (selecting f(i) in S_i for each color class i) whose convex hull conv({f(0), ..., f(d)}) contains p. Formulated over arbitrary dimension d, with specializations to the origin and low dimensions (d = 0, 1, 2), a formal deduction of the classical Carathéodory theorem bound, the 1D Centerpoint Theorem (median contains >= floor((n+1)/2) = ceil(n/2) points in each half-line), Bárány's 1982 First Selection Lemma (>= (|P|/2)(|P|-|P|/2) pairs containing the centerpoint), and the 1D Colorful Selection Lemma (at least one colorful pair covering p). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A comprehensive, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Erdős–Szekeres Convex Polygon Theorem (1935). Formalizes orientation determinants, general position, 2D rotation transformations with finite slope avoidance (rotating any finite set to have mutually distinct x-coordinates), x-coordinate sorting, cup-cap sequences with Pascal-type binomial split recurrences, halfspace separation for convex hulls, and rotation invariance of convex polygons. Proves that any finite set of at least choose(2k - 4, k - 2) + 1 points in general position in ℝ² contains the vertices of a strictly convex k-gon, verifying the Happy Ending Theorem under pure general position with no distinct-x-coordinate restriction. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: ukiyois/hs-virial-nbc-identity
records.abstract: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.

records.title: ehrlich-b/composition-algebras
records.abstract: Hurwitz's theorem (1898), dimension form: a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra over R - a unital, not necessarily associative or commutative bilinear product together with a symmetric positive-definite form whose quadratic form is multiplicative - has real dimension 1, 2, 4 or 8. R, C and H are exhibited so the class is inhabited; the classification into R, C, H and O is strictly stronger and is not part of this entry. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: savarin/lean-malliavin
records.abstract: Gaussian integration by parts and closability of the Malliavin derivative on an abstract Gaussian Banach space. Two compared theorems, zero definition holes. Challenge.lean (225 lines) states both results using only Mathlib definitions; Solution.lean bridges via definitional equality to the extracted Malliavin proof library.

records.title: shaikidris/prime-star-spectra-formalization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the ordered adjacency spectrum of finite prime-cover graphs. Its root-centred specialization proves that the square of the largest ordered eigenvalue equals pi(X) plus four times the finite prime sum of 1/(p-1), up to o(1). More generally, for every fixed finite set S of deleted primes and epsilon > 0, the same law with the explicit centre correction c(a) holds uniformly over allowed centres a <= (log X)^(1/2-epsilon). The same window admits a uniform centre--shell evolution theorem at the explicit first-exit frequency, with a finite localization-plus-phase error bound.

records.title: ehrlich-b/composition-algebras
records.abstract: Hurwitz's theorem (1898), classification form: a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra over R - a unital, not necessarily associative or commutative bilinear product together with a symmetric positive-definite form whose quadratic form is multiplicative - is isomorphic to R, C, the quaternions or the octonions, by a linear isomorphism preserving the unit, the product and the norm form. All four targets are constructed, with Degen's eight-square identity discharging the octonion composition law, so every branch of the conclusion is attained. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: BochaoKong/nullstellensatz
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Rückert's Noetherianity theorem for local holomorphic-germ rings, algebraic and genuinely geometric finite projection for analytic hypersurface germs, the holomorphic constant-rank normal form, and Rückert's local analytic Nullstellensatz in finite-family and arbitrary-ideal radical forms.

records.title: pengzhang91/Feige
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the sharp unit-slack (delta = 1) small-deviation inequality for sums of independent nonnegative random variables. For every positive integer n and every independent family X_1, ..., X_n of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables satisfying E[X_i] <= 1, writing S = sum_i X_i, it proves the sharp bound P(S < E[S] + 1) >= (n / (n + 1))^n and proves that this constant is optimal for each fixed n. This optimal dimension-dependent bound strengthens and implies Feige's 1/e conjecture. The repository also formalizes the Vlassis-Thomas exact calibration theorem and Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality used in the proof.

records.title: JD-Jones-ASES/Hadamard-formal
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the periodic Cooper-Wallis construction and of Hadamard existence at eight orders: from kernel-checked periodic T-matrix quadruples of orders 103 and 163 and seven symmetric-circulant Williamson quadruples, the development proves that Hadamard matrices of orders 2884, 4532, 7004, 7172, 7828, 8476, 9476, and 11948 exist. Each of the eight orders lands on an entry of Table 4 of Cati and Pasechnik's maintained construction database (arXiv:2411.18897v2, 2025-08-30) recording no Hadamard matrix of that order as known, and the source repositories' firsthand audit of the construction literature (closed 2026-08-29) located no published route to the order-103 or order-163 T-objects the eight are built from. The development also proves the erratum core of the companion Hadamard-M note on Miyamoto's 1991 construction paper: the handshake parity obstruction, its empty-class corollary, and the nonexistence of the displayed C2-matrix ingredient of that paper's Corollary 4 at every positive block order not congruent to 1 mod 4 - covering the paper's printed list entries at orders 103, 127, and 151 under both printed readings of the corollary's output order, and leaving the order-515 list entry, the paper's claim of a Hadamard matrix of order 2060, unsupported by the paper's own machinery. Cati and Pasechnik, for want of details, record being unable to verify the constructions claimed in that paper's section 7, naming order 4*515 as their example; the obstruction supplies an independent mathematical reason the printed route cannot deliver that entry. Order 2060 itself is not open: a Hadamard matrix of that order was posted publicly on 2026-08-23, credited to Schneider, by other means.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/GraphCoveringTheory
records.abstract: Formalizes the sharp Schreier index formula for a finite-index subgroup of a free group on a finite nonempty generating type. For a finite nonempty type alpha, a subgroup H of FreeGroup alpha with finite index d is proved equivalent, as a group, to FreeGroup (Fin (1 + d * (card alpha - 1))). More strongly, the repository exposes a FreeGroupBasis for H with this indexing type. The proof realizes H as the vertex group of the finite action-groupoid covering on the coset space, verifies the covering locally by explicit star and costar bijections, and counts the complement of a geodesic spanning tree. It also exposes the truncation-safe natural-number statement and the generic finite free-groupoid rank calculation used by the submission theorem. For finite-index normal subgroups, a companion module proves that every deck transformation of the finite Schreier action is a unique right translation by the quotient group.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Frankl–Wilson theorem (1981) for modulo-p intersecting set families. Uses the polynomial linear algebra method over ZMod p to prove both the general non-uniform bound |F| <= sum_{i=0}^s choose(n, i) and the uniform cardinality bound |F| <= choose(n, s). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: stalex444/mahler-measure-minima
records.abstract: For each degree d in {2, 3, 4}, the polynomial x^d - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer polynomials of degree d with Mahler measure above one, and the three minimal values are exactly the golden ratio (M^2 = M + 1), the plastic ratio (M^3 = M + 1), and the root of x^4 - x^3 - 1 above one (M^4 = M^3 + 1); by Siegel's classical theorem (1944, cited as background, not formalized here) the latter two are the smallest and second-smallest Pisot numbers. Classically the degree-4 minimizer is not itself a Pisot polynomial, yet its measure lands back on the Pisot list via the reciprocal transform. The minimizers' irreducibility is part of the compared surface. Proofs are by a Graeffe-certificate architecture: an effective coefficient-bound box from Mathlib's norm_coeff_le_choose_mul_mahlerMeasure, then one integer certificate per box element (tie orbit, cyclotomic cofactor, explicit factorization, or an iterated Graeffe coefficient bound), 6,171 + 147 + 21 certificates kernel-decided with plain decide — no native_decide anywhere. The exact values follow from a root-inversion identity and a (sigma, s)-reduction localizing the conjugate pairs, with multiplicity excluded by kernel-certified measure brackets.

records.title: akopjan/NRR-AAK
records.abstract: Formalization of the result by A. Akopyan, S. Avvakumov, and R. Karasev that every convex figure in the plane can be partitioned into n convex pieces having equal area and equal perimeter for any n≥1.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Lovász's Colorful Helly Theorem (1974 / Bárány 1982). Proves that for any d + 1 finite families of convex sets in R^d such that every colorful transversal has a non-empty intersection, at least one entire family has a non-empty intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem: for an arbitrary measurable space (alpha, A) and a Polish space Y, a multifunction Phi : alpha -> Set Y with nonempty closed values that is weakly measurable (the hit set {a | Phi a meets U} lies in A for every open U) admits an A-to-Borel measurable selection f with f a in Phi a for every a.  The statement is measure-free and pointwise: no measure appears, and the selection property holds everywhere, not almost everywhere.  It is proved from Mathlib alone, by the classical argument — a dense sequence in Y, a recursion producing measurable countably-valued approximate selectors whose successive stages stay within (1/2)^n, and a uniform Cauchy limit that is measurable as a pointwise limit of measurable functions and lands in Phi a because Phi a is closed.  The measurability of each refinement step is obtained by splitting over the countably many measurable fibres of the previous stage's index function, on each of which the test set is cut out by a fixed open set, so the weak measurability hypothesis applies directly.  No measurable selection theorem exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas–Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The measurable selection theorem is used in that development to produce plain-Borel-measurable feasible bicausal strategies.

records.title: yoshito-ishiki-math/lean-scottish-book-155
records.abstract: A Lean proof that there are real Banach spaces X and Y and a bijection U from X to Y which preserves every pairwise distance on every closed ball of radius one quarter while failing to be a global isometry. This gives a counterexample to Scottish Book Problem 155.

records.title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The results registered by this Comparator configuration are Choquet capacitability for analytic sets in its finite-measure form, and its immediate corollary, the universal measurability of analytic sets.  Concretely: for a Polish space X carrying its Borel sigma-algebra, a finite Borel measure mu on X, and an analytic (not necessarily Borel) set A contained in X, the outer measure of A is the supremum of mu K over the compact subsets K of A; and consequently A is null-measurable for mu, i.e. it differs from a Borel set by a mu-null set.  Both are proved from Mathlib alone.  The argument writes a nonempty analytic set as the range of a continuous map pi from Baire space, forms the Souslin scheme of closures of images of cylinders, and runs a measure-free recursion that produces, coordinate by coordinate, a bound beta with c < mu (W(beta,n)) for every n, where W(beta,n) is the closed union of the scheme pieces bounded by beta on the first n coordinates.  A subsequence extraction inside the compact set of beta-bounded branches shows that the intersection of the W(beta,n) is contained in the compact set pi '' Sigma(beta), and continuity of mu along the decreasing sequence of closed sets W(beta,n) — the one step that uses finiteness of mu — supplies the compact witness.  Universal measurability then follows by inner approximation within 1/(k+1), taking the union of the approximating compacts and comparing with a measurable hull. Neither result exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision, where inner regularity is available for measurable sets only.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection, Jankov-von Neumann uniformization, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  Capacitability is what makes the last of these possible: universal measurability of analytic sets is the ingredient behind the null-measurable Fubini step in Bertsekas-Shreve 7.48.

records.title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Polish-space structure of the space of probability measures: if X is a Polish space carrying its Borel sigma-algebra, then the space of Borel probability measures on X, with the topology of weak convergence, is again Polish — its topology is second countable and admits a complete compatible metric.  Mathlib at the pinned revision already supplies the Levy-Prokhorov metric, the identification of the Levy-Prokhorov topology with the topology of weak convergence on a separable space, and Prokhorov's theorem; it stops at metrizability of the space of probability measures and supplies neither completeness nor separability.  Both are proved here.  Completeness: a Levy-Prokhorov Cauchy sequence is uniformly tight, the compact witness being an intersection over j of finite unions of closed balls of radius 2^(-j), whose heads are covered using a countable dense sequence and continuity from below and whose tails are transferred between members of the sequence along the Levy-Prokhorov inequality; Prokhorov's theorem then produces a convergent subsequence, and a Cauchy sequence with a convergent subsequence converges.  Separability: normalized natural-weight mixtures of Dirac measures at points of a countable dense sequence are dense in Levy-Prokhorov distance.  Complete plus separable metric gives a Polish structure on the Levy-Prokhorov space, which Mathlib's homeomorphism LevyProkhorov.probabilityMeasureHomeomorph transports to the space of probability measures with the weak topology.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov-von Neumann uniformization, the Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The registered result is used in that development to make the space of probability measures a legitimate Polish parameter space for kernels and for the Bellman recursion.

records.title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Jankov-von Neumann uniformization theorem: for Polish spaces X and Y and a nonempty analytic (Sigma-1-1) set P in X x Y, there is a function phi : X -> Y that uniformizes P on its projection, (x, phi x) in P for every x in proj_X(P), and that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable, meaning that phi-preimages of Borel subsets of Y lie in the sigma-algebra generated by the analytic subsets of X.  The statement of record writes both sigma-algebras out in full, so it mentions only Mathlib notions and no bespoke definition: the domain sigma-algebra is MeasurableSpace.generateFrom {s | MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet s} (Bertsekas-Shreve Definition 7.19) and the codomain sigma-algebra is borel Y, given explicitly rather than through an ambient instance.  The proof is Kechris's own argument for 18.1: write the analytic P as the range of a continuous map from Baire space, pull it back to a closed set F in X x (N -> N), uniformize F by the leftmost branch of the section tree, and push forward.  The measurability of the leftmost branch is proved cylinder by cylinder: the preimage of a basic cylinder is a countable Boolean combination of projections of closed sets, hence lies in sigma(Sigma-1-1). Unlike the textbook proof, the Lean development never reduces the domain to Baire space, so the invariance of sigma(Sigma-1-1) under Borel isomorphism is never needed. Neither the theorem nor the analytic sigma-algebra exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas-Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  Jankov-von Neumann is the selection engine of that development: it is what produces the sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable epsilon-optimal strategies.

records.title: mrdouglasny/OSforGFF-comparator
records.abstract: Construction of the massive Gaussian Free Field in Euclidean spacetime of any dimension d >= 2 as a probability measure on the tempered distributions S'(R^d), and a proof that it satisfies all of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: OS0 analyticity, OS1 regularity, OS2 Euclidean invariance, OS3 reflection positivity, and OS4 clustering and ergodicity. The OS axioms are the conditions under which a Euclidean field theory reconstructs a relativistic quantum field theory obeying the Wightman axioms, so the free field is the base case of constructive quantum field theory on which interacting constructions are built. The development is dimension-generic: one proof parameterized by d, consuming the free covariance only through a typeclass whose per-dimension input is a single closed-form radial kernel identified with the proper-time integral, with concrete instances at d = 2, 3, 4, 5. The result addresses three research audiences. In constructive quantum field theory, the free field satisfying OS0-OS4 is the base case (Glimm-Jaffe, ch. 6) on which interacting constructions such as P(phi)_2 and phi^4_3 are built, so a machine-checked base case is the reusable starting point for any formalized interacting construction. The analytic chain is proved rather than assumed: the Minlos theorem and the Hilbert-nuclearity of Schwartz space are consumed from the bochner and gaussian-field developments as theorems, nuclearity in the general form for Schwartz functions on any finite-dimensional real normed space, so every headline result depends on nothing beyond Lean's three foundational axioms. In stochastic quantization and singular SPDEs, the massive GFF constructed here is the reference Gaussian and the invariant measure of the free dynamics in every dimension treated. And for researchers formalizing quantum field theory in various dimensions, this is, to our knowledge, the first machine-checked verification of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms — the literature search supporting that statement (scope, terms, dates, and the related-but-distinct work found) is documented in docs/novelty.md of this repository — with the dimension-generic propagator typeclass as the designed extension point for further covariances and dimensions.

records.title: Lean formalization toward Bugeaud Problem 10.61
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of criteria for Bugeaud's Problem 10.61 ([Bug12, p. 222], due to Mendès France [MF67]): for a Pisot number α > 2 and the Cantor set C(α) = {(α−1) Σ_{k≥1} ε_k α^{−k} : ε_k ∈ {0,1}}, no ξ ∈ C(α) has (ξαⁿ)_{n≥1} uniformly distributed modulo one. The problem is open; what is proved here are criteria for it and two instances. Every compared statement that concludes Problem 10.61 does so for a *quadratic* setup — a real root α > 1 of X² − aX − b whose conjugate has modulus below one — and the two instances are quadratic; the arbitrary-degree material is conditional ingredients, from which no compared statement derives non-equidistribution. Seventeen statements are compared, in four groups. (A) The reduction to symbolic dynamics is an equivalence, and it is complete. (i) Some ξ ∈ C(α) is u.d. mod 1 iff the full two-shift {0,1}^ℤ carries a shift-invariant Borel probability measure whose push-forward under an explicit factor map F is Lebesgue measure on 𝕋. (ii) 10.61 holds at α iff a finite certificate witnesses it: a mean-zero real trigonometric polynomial G on 𝕋 and a c > 0 with ∫ G∘F dμ ≥ c for every invariant μ. (iii) The pressure bracket that makes such a search terminate, −c/β ≤ ∫ g dμ over every invariant μ whenever the pressure of −βg relative to a finite partition is at most c. (B) A pressure criterion. (ii) A bounded measurable potential annihilated by every counterexample measure, an entropy floor h_min for those measures, and a partition pressure below h_min together prove 10.61 at α; and its machine form, where the potential carries a finite-state transfer bound with an integer vector certificate, the hypothesis comparing the log of the certificate ratio, less the Lebesgue mean, against h_min. (iv) The budget identity A(α)·h_min(α) = log 2, tying the Route A exponent to the floor. (C) A covering criterion for quadratic setups, and arbitrary-degree ingredients. (i) Two real inequalities — the depth slope 1 + L/R − L is negative exactly when (L−1)(R−1) > 1, and at the balanced depth M′ = ⌈M·L/R⌉ the covering total obeys an explicit logarithmic bound linear in M with that slope — and then, for a quadratic setup, a numeric certificate at depths (M, M′) yielding one open interval J ⊆ (0,1), uniform in ξ and in n, that every orbit misses at every time, whence A(α) < 1 implies 10.61 at α. (ii) For a quadratic setup of norm −b, the criterion applies exactly when (log₂ α − 1)(log₂(α/|b|) − 1) > 1. This characterizes when A(α) < 1; it does not decide Problem 10.61 for quadratic α with A(α) ≥ 1, about which nothing is compared. (iii) Three ingredients about the family Xᵈ − aXᵈ⁻¹ − 1, valid at every degree d ≥ 2: for a ≥ 3 the real root exceeding a is a Pisot number; every other conjugate has modulus at most (2/a)^{1/(d−1)}; and the numerical inequality log 2/log α + log 2/log(1/ρ) < 1 holds whenever a ≥ 2^{d+1}, a < α, ρ > 0 and a·ρᵈ⁻¹ ≤ 2. These are ingredients, not a criterion: no compared statement carries them to Problem 10.61 above degree two, because (i) is proved only for quadratic setups. At degree two the family members are quadratic setups, and the first of them is α = 2+√5. (D) The two numbers at which the machinery is run to a conclusion, both quadratic: at α = 2+√5 the strong form — an explicit interval missed by every orbit at every time — and 10.61 itself; and at α = 2+√3, 10.61 by a confinement-gap certificate. The informal account is the repository's paper.pdf: machine-written notes documenting the Lean development, not a prior paper that the development formalizes. Credit in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematics and the Lean text are the agents' work, the Fable-5 agent having written the notes and the Opus-5 agent the formalization, each directed turn by turn by Ralf Stephan, who chose the targets, selected which outputs to keep, and releases the files. He does not endorse the informal arguments and has not independently verified informal-to-formal fidelity; where the prose disagrees with the challenge file, the challenge file wins. Every compared statement depends on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and nothing else.

records.title: stalex444/Busch-theorem
records.abstract: Kernel-checked proof of Busch's theorem in finite dimension: every generalized probability measure on the effects of a complex matrix algebra — nonnegative on effects, additive whenever a sum of effects is again an effect, normalized at the identity — is represented by a unique density matrix via the trace pairing. Existence and uniqueness are both compared (busch_representation). The result is the uniqueness of the Born rule in the POVM reading; it is valid in every finite dimension (beyond finiteness and decidable equality of the index type, the compared statement assumes only [Nonempty n]) and holds already at dimension 2, where Gleason's theorem (which requires dimension at least 3) does not apply. No continuity is assumed: for a normalized measure, nonnegativity plus additivity force real homogeneity on the effect interval (scalars in [0,1]), compared separately as homogeneity_automatic. The compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.trace).

records.title: roos-j/lean-superorthogonality
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the main result (Theorem 1) of the paper  "A new type of superorthogonality" by P. T. Gressman, L. B. Pierce, J. Roos, and P.-L. Yung; arXiv:2212.08956, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 152, 665-675, 2024. The theorem provides a simple criterion on a family of functions that implies a square function estimate on Lp for every even integer p ≥ 2. This defines a new type of superorthogonality that is verified by checking a less restrictive criterion than any other type of superorthogonality previously known.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/KuroshSubgroupTheorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the sharp Schreier index formula for finite-index subgroups of free groups and the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products. The Schreier proof realizes a subgroup as the vertex group of a finite action-groupoid covering, while the Kurosh proof constructs the Bass--Serre tree, a locally bijective graph-of-groups cover, and its path-lifting normal form. The Kurosh factor-only statement is a free product of the nontrivial quotient vertex stabilizers and the free group of the quotient graph; each vertex stabilizer is identified with an intersection with a conjugate of an original factor. For finite-index normal subgroups, a companion module proves that every deck transformation of the finite Schreier action is a unique right translation by the quotient group.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Dilworth's Theorem (Robert P. Dilworth, 1950) on chain decompositions of finite posets and Mirsky's Dual Theorem (Leon Mirsky, 1971) on antichain covers. Proves that the maximum size of an antichain equals the minimum number of chains covering the poset, and dually that the maximum length of a chain equals the minimum number of antichains covering the poset. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: lean-malliavin
records.abstract: Malliavin calculus on abstract Gaussian Banach spaces, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib. The repository contains two Comparator configurations: one registered (core, via comparator.json, pinned at commit 29c57b3) and one pending (Clark--Ocone, via comparator-clark-ocone.json). The proof library (52 files) builds from Cameron--Martin quasi-invariance through the Wiener chaos decomposition and Itô isometry to the full representation formula.

records.title: Marshall Hall's theorem through finite cores
records.abstract: Formalizes Marshall Hall's finite-index free-factor theorem for finitely generated subgroups of finite-rank free groups. The proof extracts the finitely many suffix states of a subgroup generating set, completes the resulting partial generator actions to permutations of a finite state set, identifies the connected orbit with a finite core, and extends a geodesic spanning tree to obtain an inclusion-compatible free-product decomposition. The repository also proves binary and finite-indexed free-group instances of Grushko--Neumann rank additivity, the arbitrary-factor binary theorem, and the LERF consequence. The arbitrary-factor proof is carried by a finite labelled-graph fold, source-unfold, and monochromatic-vertex contraction reduction.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: The Friendship Windmill Structure Theorem (Erdős–Rényi–Sós 1966)
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Friendship Windmill Structure Theorem (Erdős, Rényi, and Sós, 1966). Proves that any finite graph in which every pair of distinct vertices shares exactly one common neighbor possesses a universal vertex w, has an odd number of vertices |V| = 2k + 1, induces a 1-regular perfect matching on V \ {w}, and is isomorphic to the Dutch windmill graph Wd(k, 2) To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: schur-numbers
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of modular Schur numbers. For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ-1). The main result proves the uniform closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n-1 for every k ≥ n-1. The development also proves the integer-to-residue formulation and lossless N ≤ m-1 bound, singleton-safety and zero-class obstructions, the exact one-color formula for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, and the stated sigma-infinity coset-cardinality bound. Mathlib-only Headline statements are checked by the Palomar Comparator configuration. A separate public 27-module hand-written, generated-independent project layer contains named canonical-cover seed count, stable-prime transport and recurrence, prime-power, and unrestricted exponent-truncation capstones; those capstones have a separate transitive-axiom audit and are outside the Comparator's statement-comparison gate. The earlier generated native_decide scan tree is excluded from the public release and verification claims.

records.title: lean-operator-theory
records.abstract: Hilbert-space operator theory from unitary power dilation through von Neumann's polynomial inequality, together with the Crouzeix--Palencia theorem that the closed numerical range is a (1 + square-root-of-2)-polynomial spectral set.

records.title: The entangled Born correlations: a mixed-state entanglement witness through the Born rule forced on the composite algebra
records.abstract: Kernel-checked entanglement package on the bipartite matrix algebra (2x2 tensor 2x2, native product index): (1) the separable-state CHSH bound 2 for the real-Pauli tuple, proved through the Bloch-disk constraint with no spectral theory; (2) an entanglement witness — a bipartite state, positive semidefinite with unit trace, that is NOT separable, with Born CHSH expectation equal to the Tsirelson value 2*sqrt(2) (the Bell state, exhibited explicitly in the Solution); (3) spectral projections without spectral theory — (1+W)/2 is an effect for every Hermitian involution W, any finite dimension; (4) the two-party correlation law forced, not postulated: for any state representing a generalized probability measure on effects (Busch's theorem vocabulary; no continuity assumed), the correlation at any pair of binary-observable settings is an explicit difference of the measure's values at two effects; (5) the assembly — a state that is not separable, is the UNIQUE state reproducing its own effect statistics (Born-rule uniqueness on the composite algebra), attains the Tsirelson value, and carries the witness correlation table XX = ZZ = 1, XZ = ZX = 0. Extended (second session, 2026-08-31) by five further compared theorems — the general bounds and the quantitative Werner-family layer: (6) the separable bound 2 at ARBITRARY finite local dimensions and arbitrary Hermitian-involution settings; (7) the state-level Tsirelson bound 2*sqrt(2) at the same generality; (8) the Werner family W_p = p|Phi+><Phi+| + ((1-p)/4)1, spelled inline from the explicit Bell projector, has CHSH expectation at most 2*sqrt(2)*p at any Hermitian-involution settings with traceless party-1 observables (p >= 0) — the Werner line of the Horodecki 1995 criterion; (9) the violation threshold: for p >= 0, W_p violates CHSH at some such settings iff p > 1/sqrt(2); (10) the separability endpoint (Werner 1989): W_p is separable for 0 <= p <= 1/3. All hypotheses are inline; the compared statements use only Mathlib vocabulary (Matrix.PosSemidef, Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.trace, the Kronecker product, Real.sqrt, Matrix.vecMulVec) with no custom definitions.

records.title: lean-spectral-theory
records.abstract: The spectral theorem for possibly unbounded self-adjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces, formalized through the Cayley transform and real projection-valued measures. The selected spectral theorem constructs a PVM whose scalar measures give the exact finite-second-moment domain and first-moment quadratic form, with measurable-set uniqueness, and is proved equivalent to equality with the unbounded coordinate spectral integral. The selected Stone theorem proves both that strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups have self-adjoint generators and that every self-adjoint operator generates such a group.

records.title: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family and Lehmer's polynomial
records.abstract: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is. Seventeen compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility.
